source.title: Étale cohomology of diamonds
source.venue: arXiv:1709.07343v4 (14 April 2026); to appear in Astérisque
source.read: arXiv v4 (14 April 2026), the 'final version to appear in Astérisque', 168 pages, PDF SHA-256 78ca42bba46f1d43c894b0dbfdfb41105efab4959ba5ba6e32e1e5cf7ef33efc, fetched 29 September 2026 and read in full by six readers in parallel (§§1–6, 7–10, 11–12, 13–17, 18–21, 22–27), whose drafts were merged, deduplicated and checked. Locators are v4 statement numbers and pages; earlier versions (v1–v3) were not compared, and the Astérisque version has not appeared.
readSections: §14 Comparison of étale, pro-étale and v-cohomology

summary: Scholze constructs the six-functor formalism for étale cohomology of diamonds and small v-stacks with torsion coefficients prime to p. Starting from spectral spaces and perfectoid spaces of characteristic p (§§2–6), he studies totally disconnected and w-local spaces and the pro-étale and v-topologies, proving that the v-topology is subcanonical with O⁺ almost acyclic (§§7–9); defines v-stacks, diamonds, spatial and locally spatial diamonds and their underlying spectral spaces (§§10–13); compares étale, quasi-pro-étale and v-cohomology and defines D_ét (§14); embeds analytic adic spaces over ℤ_p as locally spatial diamonds with the same étale site (§15); proves base change results, the four functors ⊗, RHom, f^*, Rf_* (§§16–17), proper and partially proper maps and proper base change, including invariance under change of algebraically closed base field (§§18–19); constructible sheaves and dimension theory (§§20–21); Rf_! and Rf^! with the projection formula and base change (§§22–23); ℓ-cohomological smoothness, Poincaré duality for smooth maps of adic spaces and quotients by profinite groups (§§23–24); biduality and finiteness over Spa(C, O_C) (§25); adic coefficients (§26); and the comparison with étale cohomology of schemes (§27). The atlas's diamond roadmaps were built from this text and plan almost every item: PerfectoidSpaces P0–P6, DiamondsAndVStacks D0–D6, DiamondEtaleCohomology C0–C9, DiamondSixOperations S0–S6 and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L0–L6, with ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology, AdicEtaleGeometry and EnhancedDerivedSheaves for the classical and ∞-categorical inputs. After the independent review there are 619 items (581 planned, 19 library, 19 missing). The missing items are remarks, statements made in running text, outside inputs (SGA 4 on coherent topoi, Lurie's limits of presentable ∞-categories, Neeman's criterion, Grothendieck's fppf refinement, Raynaud–Gruson over valuation rings of any height, invariance of scheme cohomology under algebraically closed field extension) and the localization Y_y; all go as sources to those layers, to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 and to AdicSpacesPartII R2. No Part II is needed. The extraction records the paper's source issues, among them errors in Lemma 7.2(iii) and Example 11.12 and gaps in Lemmas 2.9–2.10, Proposition 3.5, Proposition 14.7 and Theorem 19.5(ii), each with its correction; the stated main theorems are not affected. The review confirmed all 73 and added 28 (E74–E101), among them a false claim about algebraic topoi before Proposition 8.3, the missing hypothesis in the unbounded case of Theorem 19.2, a gap in the proof of Proposition 13.13, misprints in Theorem 1.8(iii), Proposition 22.15 and Propositions 24.2–24.3, and a false example in Remark 25.6.

items.name: §1: Perf and its analytic and étale topologies
items.statement: Perf denotes the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p. (i) The analytic topology on Perf: a cover {fᵢ : Xᵢ → X} consists of open immersions Xᵢ ↪ X which jointly cover X. (ii) The étale topology on Perf: a cover {fᵢ : Xᵢ → X} consists of étale maps Xᵢ → X which jointly cover X. (The condition that every quasicompact open U ⊂ X is covered by finitely many quasicompact opens Uᵢ ⊂ Xᵢ, imposed in the pro-étale and v-topologies, is automatic in cases (i) and (ii) as étale maps are open.)
items.note: Perf itself: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space ('Perfd … and Perf in characteristic p'). No node defines the analytic or étale topology on Perf; the stage description of DiamondsAndVStacks:D2 plans 'comparison with the analytic and étale topologies' for its pro-étale and v-sites, so the topologies are planned only implicitly there. The small étale site of one perfectoid space is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space. The intro's pro-étale and v-topologies (iii)–(iv) are restated as Definition 8.1 (outside this range).

items.name: Definition 2.1: spectral space
items.statement: A spectral space is a topological space X such that X is quasicompact, X has a basis of quasicompact open subsets stable under finite intersection, and every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point.
items.note: Mathlib's SpectralSpace is T0Space + CompactSpace + QuasiSober + QuasiSeparatedSpace + PrespectralSpace (Stacks 08YG), equivalent to 2.1; the identification is recorded in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space.

items.name: Definition 2.1: locally spectral space
items.statement: A locally spectral space is a topological space X that admits an open cover by spectral subspaces.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space (IsLocallySpectralSpace). Absent from Mathlib and Tau Ceti at the pinned commits.

items.name: Definition 2.1: spectral map of spectral spaces
items.statement: A morphism f : X → Y between spectral spaces is spectral if it is continuous and the preimage of any quasicompact open subset is quasicompact open.
items.note: Mathlib's IsSpectralMap (continuous, preimage of compact open is compact) is stated for arbitrary spaces and agrees with 2.1 on spectral spaces.

items.name: Definition 2.1: spectral map of locally spectral spaces
items.statement: A morphism f : X → Y between locally spectral spaces is spectral if it is continuous and for any spectral open subspace U ⊂ X mapping into some spectral open V ⊂ Y, the map U → V is spectral.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space (IsSpectralMap.locally and its cover criterion).

items.name: Theorem 2.2(i)–(iii) (Hochster): characterisations of spectral spaces
items.statement: Let X be a topological space. The following conditions are equivalent. (i) The space X is spectral. (ii) There is a ring A such that X ≅ Spec A. (iii) The space X can be written as an inverse limit of finite T₀-spaces.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/hochster-realization. Only (ii) ⇒ (i) is in the library: Mathlib's instance SpectralSpace (PrimeSpectrum R) (Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:842). Hochster's realisation (i) ⇒ (ii) and the inverse-limit description are missing.

items.name: Theorem 2.2: spectral spaces as the pro-category of finite T₀-spaces
items.statement: The category of spectral spaces with spectral maps is equivalent to the pro-category of finite T₀-spaces.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces (also constructs Pro(C) and Pro_κ(C)).

items.name: §2: constructible subsets and the constructible topology
items.statement: A subset T ⊂ X of a spectral space X is constructible if it lies in the boolean algebra generated by quasicompact open subsets. The constructible topology on X is the topology generated by constructible subsets. More generally, a subset T ⊂ X of a locally spectral space X is constructible if its intersection with any spectral open subspace is constructible.
items.note: Mathlib's IsConstructible is the boolean algebra generated by open retrocompact sets, which on a quasiseparated space are the quasicompact opens (QuasiSeparatedSpace.isRetrocompact_iff_isCompact); constructibleTopology is generated by compact opens and closed sets with compact complement and equals generateFrom {IsConstructible} on compact quasiseparated spaces (constructibleTopology_eq_generateFrom_isConstructible). The locally spectral version is Mathlib's IsLocallyConstructible (Stacks 005G): on a locally spectral space 'constructible in every spectral open' is equivalent to it (IsLocallyConstructible.preimage_of_isOpenEmbedding, IsLocallyConstructible.isConstructible, IsLocallyConstructible.of_isOpenCover).

items.name: §2: the constructible topology of a spectral space is profinite
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. Then X equipped with its constructible topology is a profinite set. If X is an inverse limit of finite T₀-spaces Xᵢ, then X with the constructible topology is the inverse limit of the Xᵢ equipped with the discrete topology.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite. Mathlib has only compactness (instance compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology); Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness are an explicit TODO in Mathlib/Topology/Spectral/ConstructibleTopology.lean.

items.name: §2: pro-constructible subsets (spectral and locally spectral)
items.statement: A subset T ⊂ X of a spectral space X is pro-constructible if it is an intersection of constructible subsets. More generally, a subset T ⊂ X of a locally spectral space X is pro-constructible if the intersection with any spectral open subspace is pro-constructible.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets. Tau Ceti has tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible, but it is DEFINED as closedness in the constructible topology (the characterisation of Lemma 2.3), not as an intersection of constructible sets, and has no locally spectral version; so the definition as stated is not yet in the library.

items.name: Lemma 2.3(i): pro-constructible = closed in the constructible topology
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. A subset S ⊂ X is pro-constructible if and only if S is closed in the constructible topology.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets. Tau Ceti takes the right-hand side as the definition of TauCeti.IsProConstructible, so the equivalence with 'intersection of constructible subsets' is missing.

items.name: Lemma 2.3(ii): images of pro-constructible sets under spectral maps
items.statement: If f : X → Y is a spectral map of spectral spaces, then the image of any pro-constructible subset of X is a pro-constructible subset of Y.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets. Tau Ceti has only preimages (TauCeti.IsProConstructible.preimage); the image statement needs Hausdorffness of the constructible topology, not in Mathlib.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: closure of a pro-constructible set
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space, and S ⊂ X a pro-constructible subset. Then the closure S̄ ⊂ X of S is the set of specializations of points in S.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible. Closest library result: tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible.mem_of_isGenericPoint (the generic point of the closure lies in S), which is weaker.

items.name: §2: maps of analytic adic spaces are generalizing
items.statement: All maps of analytic adic spaces are generalizing (in particular all maps of perfectoid spaces are generalizing).
items.locator: §2, sentence before Lemma 2.5, p. 11 (used again in the proof of Corollary 5.5, p. 24), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Asserted without proof. Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing ('more generally of analytic adic spaces'). No GeneralizingMap result for adic spectra in Tau Ceti.

items.name: Lemma 2.5: surjective generalizing spectral maps are quotient maps
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a surjective and generalizing spectral map of spectral spaces. Then f is a quotient map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient (uses mathlib:GeneralizingMap). Mathlib has only the special case of Spec of a ring map, PrimeSpectrum.isQuotientMap_of_generalizingMap (Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:912).

items.name: Lemma 2.6: surjections onto compact Hausdorff spaces are quotient maps
items.statement: Let f : S → T be a continuous surjective map from a quasicompact space S to a compact Hausdorff space T. Then f is a quotient map.
items.note: Mathlib: [CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y], Surjective f, Continuous f ⊢ IsQuotientMap f (Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff.lean:682). CompactSpace is quasicompactness; compactness of T is not needed. Also recorded in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient.

items.name: §2: quasiseparated topological space
items.statement: A topological space is quasiseparated if the intersection of any two quasicompact open subsets is quasicompact.

items.name: Lemma 2.7(ii): R-invariant open neighbourhoods
items.statement: Let X be a quasiseparated locally spectral space, and let R ⊂ X × X be a pro-constructible equivalence relation such that the maps s, t : R → X are quasicompact and generalizing. Then for any quasicompact open W ⊂ X, there exists an open R-invariant subset U ⊃ W such that U ⊂ E, where E is some R-invariant subset that is an intersection of a nonempty family of quasicompact open subsets.
items.locator: Lemma 2.7, second statement, p. 11 (proof pp. 11–12, following [Sta, Tag 0APA, 0APB]), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-equivalence-relation (states the result with E′ = t(s⁻¹(W′)), as the printed proof does). The proof also yields U ⊂ W′ for a chosen quasicompact open W′ ⊃ t(s⁻¹(W)), which is what later proofs use.

items.name: Lemma 2.7(i): quotients by pro-constructible equivalence relations are T₀
items.statement: Let X be a quasiseparated locally spectral space, and let R ⊂ X × X be a pro-constructible equivalence relation such that the maps s, t : R → X are quasicompact and generalizing. Then the quotient space X/R is T₀.
items.locator: Lemma 2.7, first statement, p. 11 (proof p. 12), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-equivalence-relation. Proof uses part (ii).

items.name: Remark 2.8: compact Hausdorff spaces as quotients of profinite sets
items.statement: Even if X is spectral, under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.7 the quotient X/R need not be spectral: given a compact Hausdorff space Y, let X be the Stone–Čech compactification of Y considered as a discrete set; then X is a profinite set with a natural continuous surjection X → Y, and the induced equivalence relation R ⊂ X × X is closed, hence profinite, with X/R = Y.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/profinite-presentation-of-compact-hausdorff (Mathlib has StoneCech and the CompHaus/Profinite categories, but not this presentation as stated).

items.name: Lemma 2.9: spectral quotient criterion
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space, and let R ⊂ X × X be a pro-constructible equivalence relation such that the maps s, t : R → X are generalizing. Assume that X/R has a basis for the topology given by open subsets whose preimages in X are quasicompact. Then X/R is a spectral space, and X → X/R is a spectral and generalizing map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/spectral-quotient-criterion. Its proof step 2 copies the paper's existence-of-generic-point argument, which omits intersecting with the irreducible closed set (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 2.10: quotients by open pro-constructible equivalence relations
items.statement: Let X be a quasiseparated locally spectral space, and let R ⊂ X × X be a pro-constructible equivalence relation such that s, t : R → X are quasicompact and generalizing (the situation of Lemma 2.7), and assume that R → X is open. Then the quotient space X/R is locally spectral and quasiseparated, and X → X/R is an open spectral qcqs map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/spectral-quotient-criterion (second half). Same generic-point gap as Lemma 2.9 (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Lemma 2.11(i): cofiltered limits of spectral spaces
items.statement: Let Xᵢ, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of spectral spaces along spectral maps, with inverse limit X = lim← Xᵢ. Then X is a spectral space, the maps X → Xᵢ are spectral, and a map Y → X from a spectral space is spectral if and only if all composites Y → X → Xᵢ are spectral.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces. Proof: via Pro(finite T₀) (Theorem 2.2).

items.name: Lemma 2.11(ii): generalizing maps into cofiltered limits
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 2.11(i), if Y is a spectral space with a spectral map Y → X such that the composite maps Y → Xᵢ are generalizing, then Y → X is generalizing. In particular, if Y → X is in addition surjective, then by Lemma 2.5 it is a quotient map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces.

items.name: §3: Tate rings, pseudo-uniformizers, R°, rings of integral elements
items.statement: A topological ring R is Tate if it contains an open and bounded subring R₀ ⊂ R and a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ ∈ R; such elements ϖ are called pseudo-uniformizers. R° ⊂ R denotes the set of powerbounded elements. A ring of integral elements is an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R°.
items.note: Tau Ceti's IsTateRing is 'Huber ring (has a pair of definition) with a topologically nilpotent unit'; this is equivalent to the paper's wording (R₀ with ideal of definition ϖᴺR₀). IsRingOfIntegralElements = open, integrally closed in A, contained in powerBoundedSubring A (TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Pair.lean:73).

items.name: §3: pseudo-uniformizers lie in R° and in every ring of integral elements
items.statement: If ϖ ∈ R is a pseudo-uniformizer of a Tate ring R, then ϖ ∈ R°; and if R⁺ ⊂ R is a ring of integral elements, then ϖ ∈ R⁺.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves that every topologically nilpotent element lies in any ring of integral elements (hence in R°), exactly the paper's argument.

items.name: Definition 3.1: perfectoid Tate ring
items.statement: A Tate ring R is perfectoid if R is complete, uniform, i.e. R° ⊂ R is bounded, and there exists a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R such that ϖᵖ | p in R° and the Frobenius map Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖᵖ : x ↦ xᵖ is an isomorphism.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras. No perfectoid-ring notion in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Remark 3.2: injectivity of Frobenius and the Frobenius-surjectivity criterion
items.statement: For any complete Tate ring R and pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖᵖ | p in R°, the Frobenius map Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖᵖ is necessarily injective. The condition that Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖᵖ is an isomorphism is independent of the choice of a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖᵖ | p, and, for a complete Tate ring R admitting such a ϖ, is equivalent to the condition that Φ : R°/p → R°/p is surjective.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (keeps the ϖᵖ | p hypothesis; atlas finding PerfectoidSpaces/E6 on this was rejected by review).

items.name: Remark 3.3: ℚ_p and discretely valued fields are not perfectoid
items.statement: The field ℚ_p is not perfectoid, even though the Frobenius on 𝔽_p is an isomorphism: there is no ϖ ∈ ℤ_p whose p-th power divides p. More generally, a discretely valued nonarchimedean field K cannot be perfectoid.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation; stage P1 text: 'In particular, ℚ_p is not perfectoid'.

items.name: Example 3.4: basic perfectoid Tate rings
items.statement: (i) The cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl, the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}). (ii) The t-adic completion 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) of 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}). (iii) ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ := A[1/p], A the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]. (iv) R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T], a perfectoid Tate ring not over a field, with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ϖᵖ = T divides p in R°).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples (stage P1 'Tests' list these, including 3.4(iv)).

items.name: Proposition 3.5: perfectoid rings in characteristic p
items.statement: Let R be a topological ring with pR = 0. The following are equivalent: (1) R is a perfectoid Tate ring; (2) R is a perfect complete Tate ring (perfect meaning Φ : R → R is an isomorphism).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform. The printed uniformity argument has a faulty step (see sourceIssues; atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E7). See also source issue E78 (added by the review).

items.name: Open mapping theorem (black box in Proposition 3.5)
items.statement: (Banach's open mapping theorem, as used) A continuous surjective linear map between complete metrizable topological modules over a Tate ring is open; in particular the Frobenius Φ : R → R of a perfect complete Tate ring R of characteristic p (linear for the Frobenius-twisted module structure on the target) is open.
items.note: Tau Ceti's Henkel open mapping theorem (A-equivariant additive surjection, A with a zero sequence of units, complete first-countable nonarchimedean source, Baire T₀ target) applies to Φ with A acting on the target through a ↦ aᵖ. Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap is the normed-space version. Planned use: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform lists TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap as prerequisite.

items.name: Definition 3.6: perfectoid field
items.statement: A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring R which is a nonarchimedean field.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition.

items.name: Remark 3.7 (Kedlaya): perfectoid rings that are fields
items.statement: A perfectoid Tate ring which is a field is a perfectoid field (i.e. its topology is given by a nonarchimedean absolute value).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field (with P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field).

items.name: Proposition 3.8: characterisation of perfectoid fields
items.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean field. Then K is a perfectoid field if and only if (i) K is not discretely valued, (ii) |p| < 1, and (iii) the Frobenius Φ : O_K/p → O_K/p is surjective.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation. Stated without proof ('one easily checks').

items.name: Definition 3.9: the tilt R♭
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. The tilt of R is the topological ring R♭ = lim←_{x↦xᵖ} R, with the inverse limit topology, the pointwise multiplication, and the addition (x⁽⁰⁾, x⁽¹⁾, …) + (y⁽⁰⁾, y⁽¹⁾, …) = (z⁽⁰⁾, z⁽¹⁾, …) where z⁽ⁱ⁾ = lim_{n→∞} (x⁽ⁱ⁺ⁿ⁾ + y⁽ⁱ⁺ⁿ⁾)^{pⁿ} ∈ R.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring. Mathlib has PreTilt O p := Perfection (O/p) p (and Tilt of a valued field), i.e. the integral tilt lim_Φ O/p; the comparison R♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt R⁺ p is planned in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt. The Tate-ring tilt R♭ itself is not in the library.

items.name: Lemma 3.10(i): the tilt is perfectoid; R♭° as an inverse limit
items.statement: The limit z⁽ⁱ⁾ above exists and defines a ring structure making R♭ a perfectoid 𝔽_p-algebra. The subset R♭° of power-bounded elements is given by the topological ring isomorphism R♭° = lim←_{x↦xᵖ} R° ≅ lim←_Φ R°/ϖ, where ϖ ∈ R is a pseudo-uniformizer which divides p in R°.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring.

items.name: Lemma 3.10(ii): pseudo-uniformizers with p-power roots; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭]
items.statement: There exists a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R with ϖᵖ | p in R° which admits a sequence of p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ}, giving rise to an element ϖ♭ = (ϖ, ϖ^{1/p}, …) ∈ R♭°, which is a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭. Then R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭].
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings.

items.name: §3: the sharp map and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ
items.statement: Projection to the zeroth coordinate gives a continuous, multiplicative (but not additive) map R♭ = lim←_{x↦xᵖ} R → R, f ↦ f♯. It induces a ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ, and hence an inclusion-preserving bijection between the open and integrally closed subrings of R♭° and of R°.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings. Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt is the integral sharp map (planned comparison P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt).

items.name: Lemma 3.11: rings of integral elements under tilting
items.statement: The set of open and integrally closed subrings R⁺ ⊂ R° is in bijection with the set of open and integrally closed subrings R♭⁺ ⊂ R♭°, via R♭⁺ = lim←_{x↦xᵖ} R⁺. Also R♭⁺/ϖ♭ = R⁺/ϖ.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.

items.name: Theorem 3.12: tilting homeomorphism of adic spectra
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R, with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺). The map sending x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺) to x♭ ∈ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) defined by |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)| defines a homeomorphism Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺). A subset U ⊂ Spa(R, R⁺) is rational if and only if its image in Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) is rational.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets. Tau Ceti has Spa and rational subsets (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition etc.) but no tilting. Citation-scope issue recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E12.

items.name: Theorem 3.13: tilting equivalence of perfectoid algebras
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭. Then there is an equivalence of categories between perfectoid R-algebras and perfectoid R♭-algebras, via S ↦ S♭.
items.locator: Theorem 3.13, p. 17 (external: [Sch12]; 'proved only over a perfectoid field, but the proof works in general'), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence.

items.name: Lemma 3.14(i): Fontaine's θ is a surjective ring homomorphism
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊂ R, and (R♭, R♭⁺) its tilt. There is a canonical surjective ring homomorphism θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺, Σ_{n≥0} [rₙ]pⁿ ↦ Σ_{n≥0} rₙ♯ pⁿ.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel. Mathlib has WittVector.fontaineTheta : 𝕎(PreTilt R⁺ p) →+* R⁺ and surjective_fontaineTheta, but only under [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R⁺)], [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R⁺] and surjective Frobenius on R⁺/p; the identification R♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt R⁺ p and these hypotheses for perfectoid pairs are planned (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt, P1/integral-elements-adically-complete, P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).

items.name: Lemma 3.14(ii): ker θ is generated by a primitive non-zero-divisor
items.statement: The kernel of θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺ is generated by a nonzero-divisor ξ of the form ξ = p + [ϖ]α, where ϖ ∈ R♭⁺ is a pseudo-uniformizer, and α ∈ W(R♭⁺).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (with P1/quotient-by-primitive-element).

items.name: Definition 3.15: ideals primitive of degree 1
items.statement: An ideal I ⊂ W(R♭⁺) is primitive of degree 1 if I is generated by an element of the form ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α, with ϖ♭ ∈ R♭⁺ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W(R♭⁺).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals.

items.name: Lemma 3.16: primitive elements are non-zero-divisors
items.statement: Any ξ of the form ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α, with ϖ♭ ∈ R♭⁺ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W(R♭⁺), is a non-zero-divisor in W(R♭⁺).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/distinguished-element-criterion. Printed 'α ∈ W(R⁺)' is a misprint (atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E5).

items.name: Theorem 3.17: classification of untilts
items.statement: There is an equivalence of categories between (i) pairs (S, S⁺) of a perfectoid Tate ring S and an open and integrally closed subring S⁺ ⊂ S°, and (ii) triples (R, R⁺, J), where R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, R⁺ ⊂ R° an open and integrally closed subring, and J ⊂ W(R⁺) an ideal which is primitive of degree 1. The functors are (S, S⁺) ↦ (S♭, S♭⁺, ker θ) and (R, R⁺, J) ↦ (W(R⁺)[[ϖ]⁻¹]/J, W(R⁺)/J), where ϖ ∈ R is any pseudo-uniformizer.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/marked-untilt.

items.name: Theorem 3.18: sheafiness and rational localisations of perfectoid affinoids
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R°, and let X = Spa(R, R⁺). Then O_X is a sheaf, and for all rational subsets U ⊂ X, O_X(U) is again perfectoid. Moreover, if (R♭, R♭⁺) is the tilt and X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), then for any rational subset U ⊂ X with image U♭ ⊂ X♭ (Theorem 3.12), O_X(U) is perfectoid with tilt O_{X♭}(U♭).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy. Tau Ceti has Spa(A, A⁺), its spectrality, rational subsets and analytic points, but no structure presheaf or sheafiness theorem. Citation-scope issue recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E12.

items.name: Definition 3.19: perfectoid space
items.statement: A perfectoid space is an adic space covered by open subspaces which are isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺), where R is a perfectoid Tate ring, and R⁺ ⊂ R° is an open and integrally closed subring.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space. Requires the adic-space category of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces Layer 5, which the atlas plans (stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry).

items.name: §3: the tilt X ↦ X♭ of a perfectoid space
items.statement: The tilting process glues to give a functor X ↦ X♭ from perfectoid spaces to perfectoid spaces of characteristic p, with |X| ≅ |X♭|.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting.

items.name: Corollary 3.20: tilting equivalence over a perfectoid space
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭. Then the functor X′ ↦ X′♭ from perfectoid spaces over X to perfectoid spaces over X♭ is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence.

items.name: Definition 3.21: almost zero modules
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. An R°-module M is almost zero if ϖM = 0 for all pseudo-uniformizers ϖ. Equivalently, if ϖ is a fixed pseudo-uniformizer admitting p-power roots, M is almost zero if and only if ϖ^{1/pⁿ}M = 0 for all n. The same definition applies to R⁺-modules; the condition only uses the R⁺-module structure.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal. No almost mathematics in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Example 3.22(i): almost zero modules over O_K
items.statement: If K is a perfectoid field, then the residue field k = O_K/m_K is almost zero as an O_K-module; conversely, any almost zero module over O_K is a k-vector space, and thus a direct sum of copies of k.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P0/valuation-ring-basic-setup, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup.

items.name: Example 3.22(ii): R°/R⁺ is almost zero
items.statement: If R is perfectoid and R⁺ ⊂ R° is any ring of integral elements, then R°/R⁺ is almost zero.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup.

items.name: §3: almost zero modules form a Serre subcategory
items.statement: Extensions of almost zero modules are almost zero. Thus the category of almost zero modules is a thick Serre subcategory of the category of all modules.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class.

items.name: Definition 3.23: almost modules
items.statement: The category of almost R°-modules, R°ᵃ-mod, is the quotient of the category of R°-modules by the subcategory of almost zero modules. One can also define R⁺ᵃ-mod, and the natural forgetful map R°ᵃ-mod → R⁺ᵃ-mod is an equivalence.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup (stage P0 text: 'comparison of the almost module categories from R⁺ and R°').

items.name: Theorem 3.24: almost acyclicity of O⁺ on perfectoid affinoids
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R°, and let X = Spa(R, R⁺). Then the R⁺-module Hⁱ(X, O_X⁺) is almost zero for i > 0, and H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity.

items.name: Lemma 4.1: cutoff cardinals
items.statement: There is a cofinal class of uncountable cardinals κ with the following properties. (i) For all cardinals λ < κ, one has 2^λ < κ, i.e. κ is a strong limit cardinal. (ii) For all countable sequences λ₁, λ₂, … < κ of cardinals less than κ, the supremum of all λᵢ is less than κ, i.e. the cofinality of κ is larger than ω. (iii) For all cardinals λ < κ, there is a strong limit cardinal κ_λ < κ such that the cofinality of κ_λ is larger than λ. (In (iii), the set of such κ_λ is automatically cofinal in κ.)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (stage D0: 'Prove the abstract cutoff-cardinal existence lemma of ECD 4.1 here'). Mathlib has Cardinal.IsStrongLimit, beth numbers and cofinality, but not this lemma. Note the constructed κ may be singular (e.g. κ(ω₁)), which matters for Proposition 4.4.

items.name: Definition 4.2: κ-small perfectoid space
items.statement: A perfectoid space X is κ-small if the cardinality of |X| is less than κ, and for all open affinoid subspaces U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊂ X, the cardinality of A is less than κ.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space (with the variant P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space). The paper notes that for §4 it suffices that κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal.

items.name: Remark 4.3: cardinality of a completion
items.statement: Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. If A has a dense subalgebra A₀ ⊂ A of cardinality less than κ, then A has cardinality less than κ (indeed #A ≤ λ^ω ≤ 2^λ < κ, λ = #A₀).
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality. (The printed equality 2^{λ×ω} = 2^λ needs λ infinite; the finite case is immediate since 2^ω < κ.)

items.name: Proposition 4.4: cover criterion for κ-smallness
items.statement: A perfectoid space X is κ-small if and only if X admits a cover by less than κ many open affinoid subspaces U = Spa(A, A⁺) for which the cardinality of A is less than κ.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion ('corrected for singular κ'). The 'if' direction is false as printed when κ is singular (allowed by Lemma 4.1); atlas finding PerfectoidSpaces/E40 (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 4.4 (addendum): κ-small spaces are stable under finite products
items.statement: The category of κ-small perfectoid spaces is stable under finite products.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure. Atlas finding PerfectoidSpaces/E40 records that for singular κ this needs a uniform bound (fibre products of uniformly κ-small spaces).

items.name: Definition 5.1: injection of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for all perfectoid spaces Z, the map f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective. (It is enough to check this for affinoid perfectoid Z.)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces.

items.name: Example 5.2: residue-field points are injections
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space and x ∈ X, giving i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X, where K(x) is the completed residue field at x and K(x)⁺ ⊂ K(x) the corresponding open and bounded valuation subring. Then i_x is an injection. For X affinoid, |Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| = ⋂_{U∋x} U over the rational neighbourhoods U of x, Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) is the inverse limit of these U in perfectoid spaces, and K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→_{U∋x} O_X⁺(U).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields.

items.name: Example 5.2 (addendum): qcqs spaces with a unique closed point
items.statement: If a perfectoid space X is qcqs and has a unique closed point x ∈ X, then X = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: characterisations of injections
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent. (i) f is an injection. (ii) For all perfectoid fields K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, the map f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective. (iii) |f| : |Y| → |X| is injective, and for all rank-1-points y ∈ Y with image x = f(y) ∈ X, the map of completed residue fields K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism. (iv) |f| : |Y| → |X| is injective, and f : Y → X is final in the category of maps g : Z → X for which |g| : |Z| → |X| factors over a continuous map |Z| → |Y|. In particular, given X, injections Y ↪ X are determined by the injective map |Y| → |X| (which need not have the subspace topology).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (with P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity, P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps, P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel). Proof of (iii) ⇒ (iv) uses Lemma 5.4.

items.name: Lemma 5.4: isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a qcqs map of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent. (i) f is an isomorphism. (ii) |f| : |Y| → |X| is bijective, and for all rank-1-points y ∈ Y with image x ∈ X, the induced map of residue fields K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism. (iii) For all perfectoid fields K with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is a bijection. (iv) For all algebraically closed perfectoid fields C with an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C, Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺) is a bijection.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion (proves (iv) ⇒ (ii) directly, avoiding the gap recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E30).

items.name: Corollary 5.5(i): base change of injections
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be an injection of perfectoid spaces, and X′ → X any map of perfectoid spaces. Then the pullback f′ : Y′ = X′ ×_X Y → X′ is an injection, and the map |Y′| → |X′| ×_{|X|} |Y| is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition. Proof misprint recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E50.

items.name: Corollary 5.5(ii): injections are the universally injective maps
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces. Then f is an injection if and only if f is universally injective, i.e. for all maps X′ → X with pullback f′ : Y′ = X′ ×_X Y → X′, the map |f′| : |Y′| → |X′| is injective.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-iff-universally-injective.

items.name: Definition 5.6: immersions of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if f is an injection and |f| : |Y| → |X| is a locally closed immersion. If |f| is in addition open (resp. closed), then f is an open (resp. closed) immersion.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion (and P4/open-immersion-comparison with the anchor's open immersions).

items.name: Definition 5.7(i): Zariski closed maps
items.statement: Let f : Z → X be a map of perfectoid spaces, where X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid. The map f is Zariski closed if f is a closed immersion and there is an ideal I ⊂ R such that |Z| ⊂ |X| is the locus where |g| = 0 for all g ∈ I.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion.

items.name: Definition 5.7(ii): strongly Zariski closed maps
items.statement: Let f : Z → X be a map of perfectoid spaces, where X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid. The map f is strongly Zariski closed if Z = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid, R → S is surjective, and S⁺ is the integral closure of R⁺ in S.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion.

items.name: §5: strongly Zariski closed ⇒ almost surjective on plus rings, and ⇒ Zariski closed
items.statement: If f : Z = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) is strongly Zariski closed, then R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (by [KL15, Proposition 3.6.9(c)]), so that the definition agrees with [Sch15, Definition II.2.6]; and f is Zariski closed.
items.locator: §5, paragraph after Definition 5.7, p. 24 (external: [KL15, Prop. 3.6.9(c)], [Sch15, §II.2]), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed. The atlas records that 'agrees with [Sch15, Def. II.2.6]' is only one implication (PerfectoidSpaces/E28) and that KL15 3.6.9(c) covers only ℚ_p-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces/E19 in PerfectoidSpaces--P8).

items.name: Theorem 5.8: Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed
items.statement: Let f : Z → X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a Zariski closed immersion of perfectoid spaces. Then f is strongly Zariski closed.
items.note: Stage PerfectoidQuotients:Q4 ('This yields ECD Theorem 5.8'; no Q4 node states it: the id PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed cited by other packets does not exist in the PerfectoidQuotients packet); imported by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed; also used in PerfectoidSpaces:P8. The following sentence's 'S⁺ → R⁺' is a misprint for R⁺ → S⁺ (atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E29).

items.name: Proposition 5.9: diagonals are immersions
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be any map of perfectoid spaces. Then the diagonal morphism Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an immersion.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map (affinoid case: Δ_f strongly Zariski closed as S ⊗̂_R S → S is surjective).

items.name: Definition 5.10: separated maps of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is separated if Δ_f is a closed immersion.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map.

items.name: §5: quasiseparated maps of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is quasiseparated if the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is quasicompact.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps.

items.name: Proposition 5.11: criteria for separatedness
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent. (i) f is separated. (ii) |Δ_f| : |Y| → |Y ×_X Y| is a closed immersion. (iii) f is quasiseparated, and for all perfectoid fields K with ring of integers O_K and open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K and any commutative square with Spa(K, O_K) → Y, Spa(K, K⁺) → X, there exists at most one map Spa(K, K⁺) → Y making the diagram commute.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(i) (almost purity): finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings are perfectoid
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭. For any finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (umbrella P3/almost-purity-theorem).

items.name: Theorem 6.1(ii) (almost purity): tilting of finite étale algebras
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭. Tilting induces an equivalence {finite étale R-algebras} → {finite étale R♭-algebras}, S ↦ S♭.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(iii) (almost purity): integral closures are almost finite étale
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. For any finite étale R-algebra S, S° is almost finite étale over R°.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence. Printed 'finite étale R-algebras S' (plural) recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E25. See also source issue E79 (added by the review).

items.name: Definition 6.2(i): finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is finite étale if for all open affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R⁺) = U ⊂ X, the preimage V = f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) ⊂ Y is affinoid perfectoid, R → S is a finite étale morphism of rings, and S⁺ is the integral closure of R⁺ in S.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces (analytic-adic analogue AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism). Mathlib has finite étale ring maps (Algebra.Etale, Module.Finite, CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale) but no perfectoid spaces.

items.name: Definition 6.2(ii): étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is étale if for all y ∈ Y there are open subsets V ⊂ Y, U ⊂ X with y ∈ V and f(V) ⊂ U, and a factorisation of f|_V : V → U as V ↪ W → U, where V ↪ W is an open immersion and W → U is finite étale.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces (analytic analogue AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism). Printed 'y ∈ Y' is a misprint for y ∈ V (atlas AdicEtaleGeometry/E2 = PerfectoidSpaces/E21 = PerfectoidSpaces/E41).

items.name: §6: basic properties of (finite) étale morphisms [Sch12, §7]
items.statement: A morphism of perfectoid spaces is finite étale if and only if there is a cover by open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊂ X such that the preimages V = Spa(S, S⁺) ⊂ Y are affinoid perfectoid, R → S is finite étale, and S⁺ is the integral closure of R⁺ in S. Composites, base changes, and maps between (finite) étale maps are (finite) étale. With X_fét, X_ét the categories of finite étale, resp. étale, perfectoid spaces over X, one has X_fét ≅ R_fét^op if X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale.

items.name: Theorem 6.3(i): tilting equivalence of étale sites
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭. Then tilting induces an equivalence X_ét ≅ X♭_ét.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity.

items.name: Theorem 6.3(ii): almost acyclicity of O⁺ on the étale site
items.statement: If X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then the R⁺-module Hⁱ(X_ét, O_X⁺) is almost zero for i > 0, and H⁰(X_ét, O_X⁺) = R⁺.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity.

items.name: Proposition 6.4(o): underlying space of a limit
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. Then the map |X| → lim← |Xᵢ| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces.
items.locator: Proposition 6.4(o), p. 27 (external: [Hub93a, Prop. 3.9], cf. [Sch12, Lemma 6.13(ii)]), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism.

items.name: Proposition 6.4(i): finite étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. Then the base change functors (Xᵢ)_fét → X_fét induce an equivalence of categories 2-lim→ᵢ (Xᵢ)_fét → X_fét (equivalently 2-lim→ᵢ (Rᵢ)_fét → R_fét).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation (with PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings and P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

items.name: Proposition 6.4(ii): qcqs étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. Let X_ét,qcqs ⊂ X_ét be the full subcategory of qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X (similarly for Xᵢ). Then the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-lim→ᵢ (Xᵢ)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent, P5/finite-stage-faithfulness, P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection, P5/finite-stage-fullness, P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity. See also source issue E80 (added by the review).

items.name: Proposition 6.4(iii): quasicompact separated étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. Let X_ét,qc,sep ⊂ X_ét,qcqs be the full subcategory of quasicompact separated étale perfectoid spaces over X (similarly for Xᵢ). Then the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-lim→ᵢ (Xᵢ)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent, P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage.

items.name: Proposition 6.4(iv): affinoid étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. Let X_ét,aff ⊂ X_ét,qc,sep be the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over X (similarly for Xᵢ). Then the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-lim→ᵢ (Xᵢ)_ét,aff → X_ét,aff.
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv, AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/finite-stage-approximation-char-p, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly (stage P6: 'Use A3 to prove the additional affinoid assertion ECD 6.4(iv)'). The printed proof is a sketch (atlas gap AdicEtaleGeometry/E15). See also source issue E81 (added by the review).

items.name: Proposition 6.4 (set-theoretic part): κ-smallness of limits
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces for some small index category I, and X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ], ϖ ∈ Rᵢ⁺ any compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizers for large i. If κ is as in Lemma 4.1, I is λ-small for some λ < κ, and all Xᵢ are κ′-small for some strong limit cardinal κ′ < κ, then X is κ-small.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-cardinal-bounds, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits.

items.name: Proposition 6.5(i): cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces
items.statement: Let Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Then the inverse limit X = lim← Xᵢ in the category of perfectoid spaces exists and is affinoid perfectoid, X = Spa(R, R⁺), where R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim→ Rᵢ⁺ (for some compatible choice of pseudo-uniformizer ϖ for all large enough i) and R = R⁺[ϖ⁻¹].
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs, P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid, P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice. Missing step recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E35; misprint 'inverse' for 'inverse limit' as PerfectoidSpaces/E38.

items.name: Proposition 6.5(ii): ω₁-cofiltered limits need no completion
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 6.5(i), if the index category I is ω₁-cofiltered, the maps lim→ Rᵢ → R and lim→ Rᵢ⁺ → R⁺ are bijective.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit.

items.name: Proposition 6.5(iii): countably generated approximation
items.statement: Any affinoid perfectoid space X = Spa(R, R⁺) can be written as an ω₁-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces Xᵢ = Spa(Rᵢ, Rᵢ⁺) where Rᵢ and Rᵢ⁺ are topologically countably generated (equivalently, have countable dense subsets).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition, P5/countable-perfectoid-hull. Proof gap recorded as atlas PerfectoidSpaces/E36.

items.name: §6: ω₁-cofiltered index categories
items.statement: An index category I is ω₁-cofiltered if for any countable category J with a map J → I, one can find an extension J^◁ → I, where J^◁ consists of J with one extra object ∗ with a unique map to each object of J.
items.note: I is ω₁-cofiltered iff Iᵒᵖ satisfies Mathlib's IsCardinalFiltered Iᵒᵖ ℵ₁ (every functor from a small category with fewer than ℵ₁ arrows has a cocone; ℵ₁ is regular). Used as such by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit.

items.name: Elkik / Gabber–Ramero approximation of finite étale algebras (black box in Proposition 6.4(i))
items.statement: (Elkik [Elk73], noetherian case; Gabber–Ramero [GR03, Proposition 5.4.53], general case; as packaged in [Sch12, Lemma 7.5(i)]) If A is a ring, t ∈ A a non-zero-divisor with (A, tA) a henselian pair and Â the t-adic completion, then B ↦ B ⊗_{A[1/t]} Â[1/t] is an equivalence between finite étale A[1/t]-algebras and finite étale Â[1/t]-algebras. Combined with the commutation of finite étale algebras with filtered colimits of rings, this gives 2-lim→ᵢ (Rᵢ)_fét ≅ R_fét for R the completed colimit of complete Tate rings Rᵢ.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 6.4(i), p. 27 (external: [Elk73], [GR03, Prop. 5.4.53], [Sch12, Lemma 7.5(i)]), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (GR arXiv Prop. 5.4.54 = book 5.4.53), PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings; stage P5 text: 'Prove finite étale finite-stage approximation using the henselian-pair/approximation theorem cited from Gabber–Ramero 5.4.53'. Mathlib has CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale and HenselianRing but not this theorem.

items.name: Huber's standard étale presentation (black box in Proposition 6.4(iv))
items.statement: ([Hub96, Proposition 1.7.1], valid for affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p via the pseudocoherent sheaves of [KL16]; [FS26, Proposition IV.4.19]) For any étale map f : Y → X = Spa(A, A⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic p, there is a Zariski closed immersion of sousperfectoid adic spaces Y ↪ Bⁿ_X whose ideal I is generated, in a neighbourhood of Y, by n functions f₁, …, fₙ ∈ A⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩ (as Ω¹_{Y/X} = 0 and I/I² ≅ Ω¹_{Bⁿ/X}/I); slightly perturbing the fᵢ still gives an affinoid sousperfectoid space étale over X, isomorphic to Y for close enough approximations.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 6.4(iv), p. 28 (external: [Hub96, Prop. 1.7.1], [KL16], [FS26, Prop. IV.4.19]), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding, A3/pseudocoherent-sheaf, A3/conormal-description, A3/local-equations-near-closed-subspace, A3/global-standard-etale-presentation, A3/standard-presentation-perturbation, A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p. Sousperfectoid spaces: stage AdicSpacesPartII:R5 ('Families and sousperfectoid spaces'). The printed argument is a sketch (atlas gap AdicEtaleGeometry/E15).

items.name: Definition 7.1: totally disconnected perfectoid space
items.statement: A perfectoid space X is totally disconnected if X is qcqs and every open cover of X splits, i.e. if {U_i ⊂ X} is an open cover of X, then ⊔_i U_i → X has a splitting (a continuous section).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/totally-disconnected-perfectoid-space states this definition verbatim; D1 stage text: 'Implement ECD 7.1–7.7 and 7.12–7.23'. No perfectoid spaces in Mathlib or Tau Ceti at the pinned commits.

items.name: Closed points of spectral spaces (recalled after Lemma 7.2)
items.statement: Any nonempty spectral space has at least one closed point: minimal nonempty closed subsets are points (by Zorn's lemma, using that cofiltered limits of nonempty spectral spaces are nonempty).
items.note: Read at Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Basic.lean:175: for [T0Space X] [CompactSpace X] and a nonempty closed S ⊆ X there is x ∈ S with {x} closed. Mathlib's SpectralSpace extends T0Space and CompactSpace, so S = univ gives the claim. (The atlas node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation also recalls it as a hypothesis.)

items.name: Lemma 7.2 (i)⇔(ii): split open covers vs. unique closed points (Fargues)
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. The following are equivalent: (i) every open cover of X splits; (ii) every connected component of X has a unique closed point.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation (proof steps (i)⇒(ii), (ii)⇒(i) recorded). Uses π0(X) profinite for spectral X (see the separate black-box item) and that the splitting property passes to closed subsets.

items.name: Lemma 7.2 (i)⇔(iii)⇔(iv)⇔(v)⇔(vi): cohomological characterisations
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. The following are equivalent: (i) every open cover of X splits; (iii) the functor F ↦ Γ(X, F) on sheaves on X is exact, i.e. commutes with all finite colimits; (iv) the functor F ↦ Γ(X, F) on sheaves of abelian groups on X is exact; (v) for all sheaves of abelian groups F on X, H^i(X, F) = 0 for all i > 0; (vi) for all sheaves of abelian groups F on X, H^1(X, F) = 0.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation, whose statement copies (iii) as printed. As printed, (iii) is false for disconnected X (Γ does not commute with finite coproducts); the proof only shows that Γ commutes with coequalizers, which is what (iii)⇒(iv) needs — see the source issue for Lemma 7.2 (iii).

items.name: Lemma 7.3 (i): projection to π0
items.statement: Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space. There is a continuous projection π : X → π0(X) to the profinite set π0(X) of connected components.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/components-of-totally-disconnected. Mathlib has ConnectedComponents and Profinite but not the profiniteness of π0 of a spectral space (see black-box item on components of spectral spaces).

items.name: Lemma 7.3 (ii): fibres of π are Spa(K, K⁺)
items.statement: Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space. All fibres of π : X → π0(X) are of the form Spa(K, K⁺) for some perfectoid field K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/components-of-totally-disconnected. Proof uses Lemma 7.2 and Example 5.2 (a qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point x is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)).

items.name: Lemma 7.3, converse
items.statement: If X is a qcqs perfectoid space all of whose connected components are of the form Spa(K, K⁺) for some perfectoid field K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, then X is totally disconnected.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/components-of-totally-disconnected ('Conversely a qcqs perfectoid space all of whose connected components have this form is totally disconnected').

items.name: Definition 7.4: w-local perfectoid space
items.statement: A perfectoid space X is w-local if its underlying topological space is a w-local spectral space in the sense of [BS15, Definition 2.1.1]. Equivalently, X is qcqs, for any open cover X = ⋃_{i∈I} U_i the map ⊔_{i∈I} U_i → X splits, and the subset X^c ⊂ X of closed points is closed. In particular, w-local spaces are totally disconnected.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-local-and-w-strictly-local.

items.name: Lemma 7.5: totally disconnected ⇒ affinoid
items.statement: Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space. Then X is affinoid.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/components-of-totally-disconnected ('Moreover X is affinoid'). A harmless misprint in the proof is recorded as a source issue.

items.name: Lemma 7.6: pro-constructible generalizing subsets are cut out by |f| ≤ 1
items.statement: Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space and U ⊂ X a pro-constructible generalizing subset. Then U is an intersection of subsets of the form {|f| ≤ 1} for varying f ∈ H⁰(X, O_X). In particular, U is an affinoid perfectoid space, which is moreover totally disconnected.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid. Its proof steps copy the faulty choice 'f_c in (K_c⁺)′ minus K_c⁺' (see source issue).

items.name: Intersections of sets {|f| ≤ 1} in affinoid perfectoid spaces (recalled after Lemma 7.6)
items.statement: In an affinoid perfectoid space Spa(R, R⁺), a finite intersection of subsets {|f| ≤ 1} (f ∈ R) is a rational subset, in particular an affinoid perfectoid space; an arbitrary such intersection is the underlying space of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces, which is itself affinoid perfectoid.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets (filtered intersection of rational subsets gives an affinoid perfectoid Z_𝒰 with |Z_𝒰| = ⋂U); limits from PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces.

items.name: Remark 7.7: quasicompact opens of totally disconnected spaces are affinoid
items.statement: Any quasicompact open subset of a totally disconnected perfectoid space X is affinoid.
items.note: Stated in node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid ('In particular every quasicompact open subset of X is affinoid').

items.name: Definition 7.8 (i): affinoid pro-étale map; pro-étale presentation
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces. f is affinoid pro-étale if Y = Spa(S, S⁺) and X = Spa(R, R⁺) are affinoid and one can write Y = lim←_{i∈I} Y_i → X as an inverse limit of étale maps Y_i → X from affinoid perfectoid spaces Y_i = Spa(S_i, S_i⁺) along a small cofiltered index category I. Any such presentation is called a pro-étale presentation.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map. Distinct from Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt (weakly étale maps of schemes).

items.name: Definition 7.8 (ii): pro-étale map
items.statement: A map f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale if for all y ∈ Y there are an open neighbourhood V ⊂ Y of y and an open subset U ⊂ X with f(V) ⊂ U such that the restriction f|_V : V → U is affinoid pro-étale.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map.

items.name: Product X × S with a profinite set (after Definition 7.8)
items.statement: For X = Spa(C, O_C) and a profinite set S = lim←_i S_i, a cofiltered limit of finite sets, set X × S = lim←_i X × S_i, where X × S_i = ⊔_{S_i} X.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set (also the relative form X ×_{S₀} S).

items.name: Affinoid pro-étale maps over a geometric point (after Definition 7.8)
items.statement: If X = Spa(C, O_C) is a geometric point, then any affinoid pro-étale map Y → X is of the form Y = X × S for some profinite set S.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point.

items.name: Remark 7.9 (a): Zariski closed immersions are affinoid pro-étale
items.statement: If f : Z ↪ X is a Zariski closed immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces, Z = {x ∈ X | g(x) = 0 for all g ∈ I} for an ideal I ⊂ R = O_X(X), then Z is the intersection of the rational subsets U_{f_1,…,f_n} = {|f_1|, …, |f_n| ≤ 1} over n and f_1, …, f_n ∈ I, and Z = lim← U_{f_1,…,f_n} → X is a pro-étale presentation; in particular f is affinoid pro-étale.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale.

items.name: Remark 7.9 (b): diagonals are pro-étale
items.statement: If f : Y → X is any morphism of perfectoid spaces, then Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is pro-étale (locally, for X and Y affinoid, Δ_f is a Zariski closed immersion and hence affinoid pro-étale).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/diagonals-are-pro-etale.

items.name: Proposition 7.10: affinoid pro-étale = Pro(affinoid étale)
items.statement: Fix an affinoid perfectoid space X; let X_ét^aff be the category of étale maps f : Y → X from affinoid perfectoid spaces Y and X_proét^aff the category of affinoid pro-étale maps f : Y → X. Then the functor Pro(X_ét^aff) → X_proét^aff, “lim←” Y_i ↦ lim← Y_i, is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence. Pro-categories are planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces (Mathlib has Ind but no Pro).

items.name: Proposition 7.10, κ-small part
items.statement: If X is κ-small and one restricts to κ-small objects in X_proét^aff, then this subcategory is equivalent to Pro_κ(X_ét^aff), the category of pro-systems whose index category is bounded by κ.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations. The printed proof covers only the first sentence (atlas source issue PerfectoidSpaces/E42).

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (i): composition
items.statement: Let g : Z → Y and f : Y → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale) morphisms of perfectoid spaces. Then f ∘ g : Z → X is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition and P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits (i).

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (ii): base change
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale) and g : X′ → X a map from a perfectoid space (resp. affinoid perfectoid space). Then f′ : Y′ = X′ ×_X Y → X′ is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change and P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits (ii).

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (iii): maps between pro-étale objects
items.statement: Let f : Y → X and f′ : Y′ → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale). Then any map g : Y → Y′ over X is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation, P6/affinoid-pro-etale-sections and P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits (iii).

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (iv): small limits
items.statement: For any affinoid perfectoid space X, the category X_proét^aff has all small limits.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits.

items.name: Proposition 7.12: w-localization X ↦ X^wl
items.statement: The inclusion from the category of w-local perfectoid spaces with w-local maps into the category of qcqs perfectoid spaces admits a left adjoint [read: right adjoint; see source issue] X ↦ X^wl, and the adjunction map X^wl → X is pro-étale. Here |X^wl| = |X|^wl is the w-localization of the spectral space |X| ([BS15, Lemma 2.1.10]), with O⁺_{X^wl} = (p^*O⁺_X)^∧_ϖ and O_{X^wl} = O⁺_{X^wl}[ϖ⁻¹], p : |X|^wl → |X| the projection.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization, whose statement copies 'left adjoint'. The adjunction map X^wl → X and 'final among w-local spaces over X' make it a right adjoint (source issue).

items.name: Proposition 7.12, affinoid case
items.statement: If X is affinoid, the map X^wl → X is an inverse limit of surjective maps of the form ⊔_{i∈I} U_i → X, where I is a finite set and U_i ⊂ X are rational subsets; in particular X^wl → X is affinoid pro-étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization.

items.name: Lemma 7.13: presentation of the w-localization of a spectral space
items.statement: Let X be a spectral topological space and B a basis for the topology consisting of quasicompact open subsets such that U, V ∈ B implies U ∩ V ∈ B. Let X^wl → X be the w-localization of X, and let C be the category of factorizations X^wl → T → X where T is a finite disjoint union of elements of B. Then C is cofiltered, and the natural map f : X^wl → lim←_C T is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Proof step of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization; D1 stage covers 7.12–7.23. A parenthetical claim in the cofilteredness argument is false as stated (source issue).

items.name: Lemma 7.14: w-localization and quasicompact opens
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space and U ⊂ X a quasicompact open subset. Then U^wl → X^wl is a quasicompact open embedding. If X = ⋃_{i∈I} U_i is a covering by quasicompact open subsets, then ⊔_i U_i^wl → X^wl is an open covering by quasicompact open subsets.
items.note: Proof step (general case) of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization.

items.name: Definition 7.15: strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space
items.statement: A perfectoid space X is strictly totally disconnected if it is qcqs and every étale cover of X splits.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected.

items.name: Proposition 7.16: characterisation of strictly totally disconnected spaces
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs perfectoid space. Then X is strictly totally disconnected if and only if every connected component of X is of the form Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed (and C⁺ ⊂ C an open and bounded valuation subring).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected (second sentence).

items.name: Definition 7.17: w-strictly local perfectoid space
items.statement: A w-strictly local perfectoid space is a w-local perfectoid space X such that for all x ∈ X the completed residue field K(x) is algebraically closed. In particular, a w-strictly local space is strictly totally disconnected.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-local-and-w-strictly-local.

items.name: Lemma 7.18: universally open strictly totally disconnected pro-étale cover
items.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space. Then there is an affinoid perfectoid space X̃ with an affinoid pro-étale, surjective and universally open map X̃ → X such that X̃ is strictly totally disconnected. If κ is as in Lemma 4.1 and X is κ-small, X̃ can be chosen κ-small.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover (uses P6's affinoid approximation, ECD 6.4 (iv)).

items.name: Lemma 7.19: pro-étale maps to a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space and f : Y → X a quasicompact separated map of perfectoid spaces. Then f is pro-étale if and only if for all rank-1 points x = Spa(C, O_C) ∈ X the fibre Y_x = Y ×_X x is isomorphic to x × S_x for some profinite set S_x. In this case Y is strictly totally disconnected and Y → X is affinoid pro-étale. (This applies in particular when Y is affinoid.)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base.

items.name: Definition 7.20: affinoid pro-étale and pro-étale spectral maps
items.statement: Let T be a spectral space such that every connected component is a totally ordered chain of specializations. A spectral map S → T of spectral spaces is affinoid pro-étale if the induced map S → T ×_{π0(T)} π0(S) is a pro-constructible and generalizing embedding. A spectral map S → T from a locally spectral space S is pro-étale if S is covered by spectral subsets S′ ⊂ S for which S′ → T is affinoid pro-étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps (first two sentences).

items.name: Corollary 7.22: topological description of pro-étale spaces over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. The functor sending f : Y → X to |f| : |Y| → |X| induces equivalences between (i) the category of (κ-small) affinoid pro-étale perfectoid spaces Y → X and the category of affinoid pro-étale maps S → |X| (of cardinality less than κ); (ii) the category of (κ-small) pro-étale perfectoid spaces Y → X and the category of pro-étale maps S → |X| (of cardinality less than κ). The inverse sends g : S → |X| to (S, O⁺_S := (g^*O⁺_X)^∧_ϖ, O_S := O⁺_S[ϖ⁻¹]).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps. Parts (i) and (ii) are proved together.

items.name: Proposition 7.23 (a): automatic flatness over a totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a totally disconnected perfectoid space and f : Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X any map from an affinoid perfectoid space Y. Then S⁺/ϖ is flat over R⁺/ϖ for any pseudouniformizer ϖ ∈ R.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/automatic-flatness. Key algebraic input (torsion-free ⇒ flat over a valuation ring) is in Mathlib (separate item).

items.name: Proposition 7.23 (b): faithful flatness for surjective maps
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 7.23, if moreover |f| : |Y| → |X| is surjective, then S⁺/ϖ is faithfully flat over R⁺/ϖ.
items.locator: Proposition 7.23, second paragraph, p. 38; proof pp. 38–39, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/automatic-flatness ('If moreover |f| is surjective then S⁺/ϖ is faithfully flat over R⁺/ϖ').

items.name: Definition 8.1 (i): the big pro-étale site
items.statement: Let Perfd be the category of perfectoid spaces and Perfd_κ ⊂ Perfd the subcategory of κ-small perfectoid spaces. The big pro-étale site is the Grothendieck topology on Perfd (resp. Perfd_κ) in which a family {f_i : Y_i → X}_{i∈I} is a covering if all f_i are pro-étale and for each quasicompact open U ⊂ X there exist a finite subset J ⊂ I and quasicompact open subsets V_i ⊂ Y_i (i ∈ J) with U = ⋃_{i∈J} f_i(V_i).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site. Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleTopology is the scheme-theoretic (weakly étale) notion, not this one.

items.name: Definition 8.1 (ii): the small pro-étale site X_proét
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space (resp. κ-small perfectoid space). The pro-étale site X_proét (resp. X_proét,κ) is the Grothendieck topology on the category of (κ-small) perfectoid spaces f : Y → X pro-étale over X, with covers the same as in the big pro-étale site.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site.

items.name: Definition 8.1 (iii): the v-site
items.statement: The v-site is the Grothendieck topology on Perfd (resp. Perfd_κ) in which a family {f_i : Y_i → X}_{i∈I} is a covering if for each quasicompact open U ⊂ X there exist a finite subset J ⊂ I and quasicompact open subsets V_i ⊂ Y_i (i ∈ J) with U = ⋃_{i∈J} f_i(V_i).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site.

items.name: Proposition 8.2: independence of the cutoff cardinal
items.statement: For any κ, κ′ as in Lemma 4.1 (κ ≤ κ′) and any κ-small perfectoid space X, the pullback functor c^*_{κ,κ′} from sheaves on X_proét,κ to sheaves on X_proét,κ′ is fully faithful and preserves cohomology: for any sheaf of sets (resp. of groups, resp. of abelian groups) F on X_proét,κ, the map F → c_{κ,κ′,*} c^*_{κ,κ′} F is an isomorphism (resp. and R¹c_{κ,κ′,*} c^*_{κ,κ′} F = 0, resp. and R^i c_{κ,κ′,*} c^*_{κ,κ′} F = 0 for all i > 0). The similar result holds for pro-étale or v-cohomology on Perfd_κ, Perfd_κ′ and their slices.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence. The first step of the printed proof (κ-filtered presentation) is recorded as defective: atlas source issues PerfectoidSpaces/E34 and E43.

items.name: Small sheaves on large sites (after Proposition 8.2)
items.statement: The category of small sheaves on X_proét is X̃_proét := lim→_κ X̃_proét,κ, the filtered colimit over cutoff cardinals κ along the pullback functors c^*_{κ,κ′} (for a small site S, S̃ denotes its category of sheaves); it is generated under small colimits by the sheaves represented by objects of X_proét. Similarly for the other large sites (the big pro-étale and v-sites on Perfd).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence ('one defines the category of small sheaves as the filtered colimit over all kappa').

items.name: Smallness criterion via ω₁-filtered colimits (after Proposition 8.2)
items.statement: If F is a sheaf which commutes with ω₁-filtered colimits, i.e. for any ω₁-filtered diagram of perfectoid pairs (R_i, R_i⁺) with colimit (R, R⁺) the map lim→_i F(Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)) → F(Spa(R, R⁺)) is an isomorphism, then F is small (it arises via pullback from the κ-small site for any uncountable κ).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence ('a sheaf commuting with omega_1-filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid rings is small').

items.name: Quasicompact and quasiseparated objects and maps in a topos (SGA 4 VI 1.1, 1.7, 1.13)
items.statement: Let T be a topos. (i) X ∈ T is quasicompact if for every family of maps f_i : X_i → X (i ∈ I) with ⊔_i X_i → X surjective there is a finite J ⊂ I with ⊔_{i∈J} X_i → X surjective. (ii) X ∈ T is quasiseparated if for all quasicompact Y, Z ∈ T over X, Y ×_X Z is quasicompact. (iii) f : Y → X is quasicompact if Z ×_X Y is quasicompact for all quasicompact Z ∈ T over X. (iv) f : Y → X is quasiseparated if Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is quasicompact. qcqs = quasicompact and quasiseparated; the same definitions are used for the categories X̃_proét of small sheaves on large sites.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos ('Mathlib has no such notions at the pinned commit').

items.name: Algebraic topos (SGA 4 VI Définition 2.3)
items.statement: A topos T is algebraic if there is a generating full subcategory C ⊂ T consisting of qcqs objects, stable under fibre products, such that for X ∈ C the map X → ∗ is quasiseparated.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos.

items.name: SGA 4 VI Corollaires 1.17, 2.6, 2.8: checking qc/qs on a generating subcategory (black box)
items.statement: Let T be an algebraic topos with generating subcategory C as above. Then quasicompactness/quasiseparatedness may be checked after pullback to objects of C and after one cover by objects of C: X ∈ T is quasiseparated iff for one cover of X by objects X_i ∈ C all X_i ×_X X_j are quasicompact (Cor. 1.17); f : Y → X is quasiseparated iff Y ×_X Z is quasiseparated for all Z ∈ C with a map Z → X (Cor. 2.6), iff Y ×_X Z is quasiseparated for all quasiseparated Z ∈ T with a map Z → X (Cor. 2.8).
items.note: External black box (SGA 4 VI). DiamondsAndVStacks D0 stage: 'Build the missing coherent and algebraic topos interfaces, qc and qs objects versus morphisms'; node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos lists them in its API (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isQuasiseparated_iff_of_cover, 'SGA 4 VI Corollaries 1.17, 2.6 and 2.8'), and the D0 packet records as a gap that SGA 4 VI was not read and these corollaries must be proved or transcribed.

items.name: Objects vs. maps to the final object (warning before Proposition 8.3; SGA 4 VI Prop. 1.3, 2.2)
items.statement: In an algebraic topos T (for the second implication, assuming that ∗ admits a surjection from some quasicompact object Y, as it does for sheaves on Perfd; the paper asserts it in every algebraic topos, where it fails, E83): if X is quasiseparated then X → ∗ is quasiseparated; if X → ∗ is quasicompact then X is quasicompact (choose a quasicompact Y with Y → ∗ surjective; then X × Y → X is a cover with X × Y quasicompact). If ∗ is not quasiseparated (as for sheaves on Perfd), the converse implications fail in general.
