items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos cites this warning in its sources; D0 stage: 'qc and qs objects versus morphisms'. The printed argument says 'any quasicompact object Y', which must be one covering ∗. See also source issue E83 (added by the review).

items.name: Proposition 8.3: the sheaf categories on Perfd and X_proét are algebraic
items.statement: The categories of small sheaves on Perfd for either the (big) pro-étale or the v-topology, and the category of small sheaves on X_proét for a perfectoid space X, are algebraic. A basis of qcqs objects stable under fibre products is in all cases given by affinoid perfectoid spaces. Moreover, a perfectoid space X is quasicompact resp. quasiseparated in any of these settings if and only if |X| is quasicompact resp. quasiseparated.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/perfectoid-sheaf-topoi-are-algebraic. The printed proof is 'Left to the reader' (source issue; also noted in the D0 coverage of the DiamondsAndVStacks packet).

items.name: Convention 8.4: quasiseparated maps of stacks
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of stacks on a topos T is called quasiseparated if Δ_f : Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is quasicompact and quasiseparated (following [Sta, Tag 04YW]; the second condition is not automatic for stacks, as the diagonal need not be injective).
items.note: Stated in node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/perfectoid-sheaf-topoi-are-algebraic.

items.name: Proposition 8.5 (i): pro-étale vs. étale comparison
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space and ν : X_proét → X_ét the natural map of sites. For any sheaf F on X_ét, the adjunction map F → ν_*ν^*F is an isomorphism. If F is a sheaf of abelian groups, then R^iν_*ν^*F = 0 for all i ≥ 1.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves. Proof follows [BS15, Corollary 5.1.6].

items.name: Proposition 8.5 (ii): sections of ν^*F on affinoid pro-étale objects
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space, Y = lim←_i Y_i → X_0 ⊂ X a pro-étale presentation of an affinoid pro-étale map Y → X_0 to an affinoid open subset X_0 ⊂ X, and F a sheaf on X_ét. Then the natural map lim→_i F(Y_i) → (ν^*F)(Y) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves. Proof follows [BS15, Lemma 5.1.1]; notational misprint in the displayed equalizer computation (source issue).

items.name: Proposition 8.5 (iii): O and O⁺ on X_proét
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space. The presheaves O, O⁺ on X_proét sending Y to O_Y(Y) resp. O⁺_Y(Y) are small sheaves. If X is affinoid perfectoid, then H^i(X_proét, O) = 0 for i > 0, and H^i(X_proét, O⁺) is almost zero for i > 0.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves; inputs [Sch12, Prop. 7.13] via PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity and P0's completion/lim¹ lemmas.

items.name: Corollary 8.6: structure sheaves and subcanonicity for the big pro-étale site
items.statement: The presheaves O : X ↦ O_X(X) and O⁺ : X ↦ O⁺_X(X) on the big pro-étale site are small sheaves. Moreover, the big pro-étale site is subcanonical, i.e. for every perfectoid space X the functor Y ↦ Hom(Y, X) is a small sheaf for the big pro-étale site.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/subcanonicity-of-the-pro-etale-topology.

items.name: Theorem 8.7: v-descent of functions; the v-site is subcanonical
items.statement: The presheaves O : X ↦ O_X(X) and O⁺ : X ↦ O⁺_X(X) on the v-site are small sheaves. Moreover, the v-site is subcanonical.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions.

items.name: Proposition 8.8: higher v-acyclicity of O and O⁺ on affinoids
items.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space. Then H^i_v(X, O) = 0 for i > 0, and H^i_v(X, O⁺) is almost zero for i > 0.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/higher-v-acyclicity; almost Amitsur/Čech inputs PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact, P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion, P0/almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion.

items.name: Definition 9.1: descent data F(Y/X) for a prestack
items.statement: Let C be a site with fibre products and F a prestack on C, i.e. a functor from C^op to groupoids. For f : Y → X in C with projections p_1, p_2 : Y ×_X Y → Y and p_12, p_13, p_23 : Y ×_X Y ×_X Y → Y ×_X Y, put F(Y/X) := {(s, α) | s ∈ F(Y), α : p_1^*(s) ≅ p_2^*(s) in F(Y ×_X Y), p_23^*α ∘ p_12^*α = p_13^*α}, with the natural functor F(X) → F(Y/X), t ↦ (f^*t, the canonical identification p_1^*f^*t = p_2^*f^*t). If f is a covering and F is a stack, F(X) → F(Y/X) is an equivalence.
items.note: Read at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/DescentData.lean: for a pseudofunctor F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Cat and a family f_i : X_i → S, DescentData consists of objects over the X_i and compatible morphisms over every object mapping to two of them (hom_self, hom_comp cocycle). For the one-element family {f} this is equivalent to Scholze's (s, α)-description when C has fibre products, but that comparison is not in Mathlib (its TODO lists 'variants when C has pullbacks'). The DiamondsAndVStacks packet (node D0/stackification) plans to reuse this Mathlib API and to add stackification; hence 'library' with this caveat.

items.name: Lemma 9.2: v-descent of morphisms of perfectoid spaces is fully faithful
items.statement: Let F be the prestack on the category of perfectoid spaces sending X to the groupoid of perfectoid spaces over X. Let X be a perfectoid space and Y → X a v-cover. Then the functor F(X) → F(Y/X) is fully faithful.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/descent-prestacks-of-perfectoid-spaces (follows from subcanonicity, Theorem 8.7).

items.name: Proposition 9.3: effective v-descent of affinoids over a totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let F be the prestack on the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces sending X to the groupoid of affinoid perfectoid spaces over X. Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space and Y → X a v-cover, where Y is an affinoid perfectoid space. Then F(X) → F(Y/X) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected; inputs PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent and P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence. Citation-scope gap already recorded as PerfectoidSpaces/E8.

items.name: Lemma 9.4: subsets whose preimage is cut out by functions
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a totally disconnected affinoid perfectoid space, X̃ = Spa(R̃, R̃⁺) an affinoid perfectoid space over X, and A ⊂ |X̃| a subset. Assume that there is a surjective map Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X such that the preimage B of A in |Ỹ|, where Ỹ = X̃ ×_X Y = Spa(S̃, S̃⁺), is an intersection of subsets of the form {|g| ≤ 1} for elements g ∈ S̃. Then A is an intersection of subsets of the form {|f| ≤ 1} for elements f ∈ R̃.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/descended-subsets-are-cut-out-by-functions. Misprint s_ij ∈ S (should be S⁺) in the proof (source issue). See also source issue E84 (added by the review).

items.name: Lemma 9.5: sections of open subsets of the closed ball over (C, C⁺)
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C. Let V be an open subset of Spa(C⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩, C⁺⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩) mapping surjectively to Spa(C, C⁺). Then there is a section Spa(C, C⁺) → V.
items.note: Acceptance item of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/descended-subsets-are-cut-out-by-functions; D3 stage: 'the section lemma for rational opens of balls over (C,C⁺) … require proofs'. Its three black-box inputs ([Gro68], Raynaud–Gruson finite presentation, lifting of special-fibre points) are listed separately and are not planned. Note: Lemma 9.4 applies it to a perfectoid ball C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (characteristic p), which needs the passage through the homeomorphism with the ordinary ball, not spelled out in the paper. See also source issue E85 (added by the review).

items.name: Proposition 9.6: effective v-descent of separated pro-étale spaces over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let F be the prestack on the category of perfectoid spaces sending a perfectoid space X to the groupoid of separated pro-étale perfectoid spaces over X. Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space and Y → X a v-cover. Then F(X) → F(Y/X) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-separated-pro-etale (uses ECD Lemma 2.7 via D0/pro-constructible-equivalence-relation).

items.name: Proposition 9.7: separated étale and finite étale spaces form v-stacks
items.statement: The prestack on the category of perfectoid spaces sending any perfectoid space X to the groupoid of separated étale perfectoid spaces over X is a stack in the v-topology. Similarly, the prestack sending X to the groupoid of finite étale perfectoid spaces over X is a stack in the v-topology.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks. The two statements are proved simultaneously.

items.name: Lemma 9.8: local isomorphisms descend along surjective generalizing spectral maps
items.statement: Let f : S′ → S be a map of spectral spaces, and let p : S̃ → S be a surjective, spectral and generalizing map of spectral spaces, with pullback f̃ : S̃′ = S′ ×_S S̃ → S̃. If f̃ is a local isomorphism, then f is a local isomorphism.
items.note: Named in the proof steps of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks ('ECD Lemma 9.8'); D3 stage: 'Prove ECD 9.2–9.11'. Uses Lemma 2.5 (D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient) and that topological fibre products of spectral spaces along spectral maps are spectral.

items.name: Lemma 9.9: compactification of qc separated étale maps to Spa(K, K⁺)
items.statement: Let X = Spa(K, K⁺), where K is a perfectoid field and K⁺ ⊂ K is an open and bounded integrally closed subring (not necessarily a valuation subring). Let Y → X be a quasicompact separated étale map. Then there is a functorial factorization Y ↪ Ȳ → X, where Y ↪ Ȳ is a quasicompact open immersion and Ȳ → X is finite étale.
items.note: Acceptance item of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks. Remark 9.10: a special case of the canonical compactification of Proposition 18.6.

items.name: Corollary 9.11 (i): pro-étaleness descends over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces and X̃ → X a v-cover, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ = Y ×_X X̃ → X̃. If f̃ is pro-étale and X is strictly totally disconnected, then f is pro-étale.
items.note: Stated in node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks ('if f tilde is pro-etale and X is strictly totally disconnected then f is pro-etale').

items.name: Corollary 9.11 (ii): étaleness is v-local on the target
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces and X̃ → X a v-cover, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ → X̃. If f̃ is étale, then f is étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks.

items.name: Corollary 9.11 (iii): finite étaleness is v-local on the target
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a map of perfectoid spaces and X̃ → X a v-cover, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ → X̃. If f̃ is finite étale, then f is finite étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks.

items.name: Definition 10.1 (i) with Convention 10.2: quasi-pro-étale maps of pro-étale stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of pro-étale stacks on Perfd, assumed locally separated (there is an open cover of Y′ over which f becomes separated; by Convention 10.2 this is part of the definition). Then f is quasi-pro-étale if for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a map X → Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y X is representable and Y′ ×_Y X → X is pro-étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks.

items.name: Definition 10.1 (ii): étale maps of pro-étale stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a locally separated map of pro-étale stacks on Perfd. Then f is étale if for any perfectoid space X with a map X → Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y X is representable and Y′ ×_Y X → X is étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks.

items.name: Definition 10.1 (iii): finite étale maps of pro-étale stacks
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks on Perfd is finite étale if for any perfectoid space X with a map X → Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y X → X is representable and finite étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks.

items.name: Automatic local separatedness (after Definition 10.1)
items.statement: If Y′ is a perfectoid space and Y is a v-sheaf, then any map f : Y′ → Y is locally separated.
items.note: Recorded as a hypothesis of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks ('A map is automatically locally separated if Y′ is a perfectoid space and Y is a v-sheaf'); stated without proof in the paper.

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (a): étale and finite étale agree for perfectoid spaces
items.statement: Let f : X′ → X be a map of perfectoid spaces. Then f is étale, resp. finite étale, if and only if the corresponding map of pro-étale sheaves on Perfd is étale, resp. finite étale.
items.note: Proof step of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks ('Record ECD Proposition 10.3'). Stated as immediate; the 'only if' direction uses base change, the 'if' direction takes X → X itself.

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (b): pro-étale = quasi-pro-étale over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let f : X′ → X be a map of perfectoid spaces with X strictly totally disconnected. Then f is pro-étale if and only if the corresponding map of pro-étale sheaves on Perfd is quasi-pro-étale. (Any pro-étale map of perfectoid spaces is quasi-pro-étale; the converse need not hold for general X.)
items.locator: Proposition 10.3 and preceding remark, p. 50, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks (proof steps and acceptance).

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (i): composition
items.statement: Let f : Y_1 → Y_2 and g : Y_2 → Y_3 be morphisms of pro-étale stacks on Perfd with composite h = g ∘ f. If f and g are quasi-pro-étale (resp. étale, finite étale), then so is h.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks ('Prove the permanence properties: composition, …').

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (ii): cancellation
items.statement: Let f : Y_1 → Y_2 and g : Y_2 → Y_3 be morphisms of pro-étale stacks on Perfd with composite h = g ∘ f. If g and h are quasi-pro-étale (resp. étale, finite étale), then so is f.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks (two-out-of-three in this direction).

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (iii): base change
items.statement: Any pullback of a quasi-pro-étale (resp. étale, finite étale) map of pro-étale stacks on Perfd is quasi-pro-étale (resp. étale, finite étale).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks.

items.name: Proposition 10.5: sub-v-sheaves of totally disconnected spaces are ind-representable
items.statement: Let X be a totally disconnected perfectoid space and Y ⊂ X a sub-v-sheaf. Then Y is ind-representable. More precisely, Y is a filtered colimit of Y_i ⊂ Y ⊂ X which are pro-constructible and generalizing subsets of X, in particular affinoid pro-étale over X.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/sub-v-sheaves-of-totally-disconnected-spaces.

items.name: Corollary 10.6: quasicompact injections are quasi-pro-étale
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a quasicompact injection of v-stacks. Then f is quasi-pro-étale, and for every totally disconnected perfectoid space X mapping to Y, the fibre product Y′ ×_Y X is representable by a pro-constructible and generalizing subset of X.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/sub-v-sheaves-of-totally-disconnected-spaces.

items.name: Definition 10.7 (i): open immersions of pro-étale stacks
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks is an open immersion if for every perfectoid space X mapping to Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y X → X is representable by an open immersion.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness.

items.name: Definition 10.7 (ii): closed immersions of pro-étale stacks
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks is a closed immersion if for every totally disconnected perfectoid space X mapping to Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y X ⊂ X is representable by a closed immersion.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness.

items.name: Definition 10.7 (iii): separated maps and separated stacks
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks is separated if Δ_f : Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is a closed immersion. A pro-étale stack Y is separated if Y → ∗ is separated.
items.locator: Definition 10.7 (iii) and last sentence, p. 51, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness.

items.name: Definition 10.7 (iv): 0-truncated maps
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks is 0-truncated if for all X ∈ Perfd the map of groupoids f(X) : Y′(X) → Y(X) is faithful.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness.

items.name: Characterisations of 0-truncatedness (after Remark 10.8)
items.statement: For a map f : Y′ → Y of pro-étale stacks the following are equivalent: f is 0-truncated; for all affinoid perfectoid spaces (or all pro-étale sheaves) X mapping to Y, the pro-étale stack Y′ ×_Y X is discrete, i.e. a pro-étale sheaf; Δ_f : Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is an injection. In particular, separated maps are 0-truncated.
items.note: Hypothesis of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness ('0-truncatedness is equivalent to …; separated maps are 0-truncated'). Stated without proof.

items.name: Remark 10.8: a separated, non-quasiseparated diamond
items.statement: Let X be a nonempty perfectoid space of characteristic p with absolute Frobenius φ. Then Y = X/φ^ℤ is a diamond which is separated but not quasiseparated (Y quasiseparated and Y → ∗ quasiseparated do not coincide).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness (hypotheses and acceptance: 'a required non-example'). Stated without proof in the paper.

items.name: Compatibility of Definition 10.7 with §5 for perfectoid spaces (after Remark 10.8)
items.statement: For a map of perfectoid spaces f : X′ → X, the notions of open immersion, closed immersion, separatedness (and 0-truncatedness) of Definition 10.7 are equivalent to the previously defined notions for perfectoid spaces (Definitions 5.6, 5.10).
items.note: Proof step of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness ('Prove that for a map of perfectoid spaces they agree with the previously defined notions of P4'). Stated without proof in the paper.

items.name: Proposition 10.9: valuative criterion for separatedness of v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks. Then f is separated if and only if f is 0-truncated, quasiseparated, and for every perfectoid field K with ring of integers O_K and open and bounded valuation subring K⁺, and every commutative square Spa(K, O_K) → Y′, Spa(K, K⁺) → Y (compatible with f), there exists at most one dotted arrow Spa(K, K⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute.
items.note: Proof step of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness ('Prove the valuative criterion …'). Perfectoid-space version is ECD Prop. 5.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness).

items.name: Proposition 10.10: uniqueness of extensions from Spa(R, R°)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks, and let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R°. Then for any commutative square Spa(R, R°) → Y′, Spa(R, R⁺) → Y (compatible with f), there exists at most one dotted arrow Spa(R, R⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute.
items.note: Proof step of node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness ('Prove the version for general pairs'); the perfectoid-space case is node PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (o): quasicompactness/quasiseparatedness is v-local on the target
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks, g : Ỹ → Y a surjective map of v-stacks, and f̃ : Ỹ′ = Ỹ ×_Y Y′ → Ỹ the pullback of f. If f̃ is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated), then f is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (i): open/closed immersions are v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 10.11 (g : Ỹ → Y surjective, f̃ the pullback of f : Y′ → Y), if f̃ is an open (resp. closed) immersion, then f is an open (resp. closed) immersion.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (ii): separatedness is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 10.11, if f̃ is separated, then f is separated.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (iii): finite étaleness is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 10.11, if f̃ is finite étale, then f is finite étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (iv): separated étale is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 10.11, if f̃ is separated and étale, then f is separated and étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (v): separated quasi-pro-étale is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 10.11, if f̃ is separated and quasi-pro-étale, then f is separated and quasi-pro-étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes.

items.name: The v-sheaf T̲ attached to a topological space
items.statement: For a topological space T, the associated v-sheaf T̲ on Perfd is given by T̲(X) = C⁰(|X|, T).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/locally-profinite-torsors (proof step: check that T̲ is a v-sheaf via Lemma 2.5).

items.name: Definition 10.12: G̲-torsors for a locally profinite group G
items.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group. A G̲-torsor is a map f : X̃ → X of v-stacks with an action of G̲ on X̃ over X such that, v-locally on X, there is a G̲-equivariant isomorphism X̃ ≅ G̲ × X.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/locally-profinite-torsors. Related special case (profinite G, consumer of D3): PerfectoidSpaces:P9/profinite-galois-tower. Grammar slip 'is map' recorded as PerfectoidSpaces/E21 (P8 packet).

items.name: Lemma 10.13: representability and pro-étale presentation of G̲-torsors
items.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group, X a perfectoid space and f : X̃ → X a G̲-torsor. Then the v-sheaf X̃ is representable by a perfectoid space, and X̃ → X is pro-étale, universally open and a v-cover. More precisely, for any open subgroup K ⊂ G, pushout along the discrete G-set G/K defines a separated étale map X̃_K := X̃ ×^{G̲} G/K → X; the transition map X̃_{K′} → X̃_K is finite étale if K′ ⊂ K is of finite index; and X̃ = lim←_K X̃_K.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/locally-profinite-torsors (its proof steps copy the imprecise 'every open subspace comes from some X̃_K'; source issue). Related results: [Han16].

items.name: [BS15, Definition 2.1.1]: w-local spectral spaces (black box)
items.statement: A spectral space X is w-local if every open cover of X splits and the subset X^c ⊂ X of closed points is closed.
items.locator: Used in Definition 7.4, p. 30 (and Lemma 7.13, p. 34), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: External definition; node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-local-and-w-strictly-local states it for perfectoid spaces ('equivalently if X is qcqs, every open cover splits, and the subset X^c of closed points is closed'). Not in Mathlib.

items.name: [BS15, Lemma 2.1.10]: w-localization of spectral spaces (black box)
items.statement: The inclusion of w-local spectral spaces with w-local maps into spectral spaces with spectral maps admits a right adjoint X ↦ X^wl; π0(X^wl) ≅ X^cons (X with the constructible topology), and the connected component of X^wl over x ∈ X is the localization X_x (the set of generalizations of x), so that points of X^wl are pairs (x, y) with y ∈ X_x and X^wl → X is (x, y) ↦ y.
items.locator: Used in Proposition 7.12, p. 34, Lemma 7.13 (proof), p. 34 and Lemma 7.14 (proof), p. 35, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization uses it ('Take the w-localization |X|^wl of the spectral space |X|'; acceptance lists π0(X^wl) = |X|_cons and components X_x), but no node constructs the topological w-localization itself and BS15 was not read into the packet. Not in Mathlib.

items.name: Connected components of spectral spaces (used in Lemmas 7.2, 7.3)
items.statement: In a spectral space X, every connected component is an intersection of open and closed subsets, and π0(X) (with the quotient topology) is a profinite set.
items.locator: used in Lemmas 7.2, 7.3, p. 30, Example 11.12, p. 58, and Propositions 11.26, 12.20 and Lemma 11.27 (also Proposition 11.30), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Used in proof steps of DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation ('pi_0 X is profinite') and D1/components-of-totally-disconnected, but no stage or node states it; D0 plans only profiniteness of the constructible topology. Mathlib has it only for compact Hausdorff spaces (ConnectedComponents.t2, connectedComponent_eq_iInter_isClopen need [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X]).

items.name: Quasicompactness of the constructible topology (used throughout §§7, 9)
items.statement: For a spectral space X, X with the constructible topology is quasicompact; in particular pro-constructible subsets are quasicompact in the constructible topology.
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Lemmas 7.5, 7.6, 7.13, 9.4, pp. 31–46, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Read at Mathlib/Topology/Spectral/ConstructibleTopology.lean:142: instance CompactSpace (WithConstructibleTopology X) under [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSober X] [PrespectralSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X], i.e. for spectral X. Hausdorffness of the constructible topology is not in Mathlib (planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite).

items.name: Cofiltered limits of nonempty spectral spaces are nonempty (used in Lemma 7.2 remark, Lemma 7.13)
items.statement: A cofiltered limit of nonempty spectral spaces along spectral maps is nonempty (Tychonoff applied to the constructible topologies).
items.locator: §7, remark after Lemma 7.2, p. 30; proof of Lemma 7.13, p. 35, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Follows from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite (constructible topology compact Hausdorff; planned) together with Mathlib's TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system (read at Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Konig.lean:126). No node plans the nonemptiness as a statement (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation only recalls it in its hypotheses, and D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces uses the same Tychonoff argument in a proof step); D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces covers spectrality of the limit.

items.name: Torsion-free modules over a valuation ring are flat (used in Proposition 7.23)
items.statement: If V is a valuation ring and M is a torsion-free V-module, then M is flat over V.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 7.23, p. 38, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Read at Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/TorsionFree.lean:93: over a Bézout domain, Flat R M ↔ torsion R M = ⊥; Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationRing.lean:381 gives the instance ValuationRing R → IsBezout R.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of elements (used in Theorem 8.7)
items.statement: If R → S is faithfully flat, then R is the equalizer of the two maps S ⇉ S ⊗_R S.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 8.7, p. 43, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Read at Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/IncludeLeftSubRight.lean:89–150: IsEffective R S (exactness of R → S → S ⊗_R S) holds for faithfully flat S, and the equalizer of s ↦ s ⊗ 1, s ↦ 1 ⊗ s is the image of R. The almost version needed in 8.7–8.8 is PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact.

items.name: Exactness of the Amitsur complex for faithfully flat maps (used in Proposition 8.8)
items.statement: If R → S is faithfully flat, the augmented Amitsur complex 0 → R → S → S ⊗_R S → S ⊗_R S ⊗_R S → ⋯ is exact.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 8.8, p. 43, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact (stated for almost faithfully flat maps, honest case included). Mathlib has only the degree-0 part (previous item).

items.name: [GR03, §3.4.1]: faithfully flat descent in the almost world (black box)
items.statement: Let A → B be a faithfully flat map of almost algebras (e.g. (R⁺/ϖ)^a → (S⁺/ϖ)^a). Then A-algebras (and A-modules) are equivalent to B-algebras (modules) with descent data relative to A.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 9.3, p. 44, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent; P0 stage: 'Prove descent for almost modules and almost algebras along faithfully flat maps'.

items.name: [Sch12, Definition 5.1 (iii), Theorem 5.2]: perfectoid algebras vs. perfectoid almost algebras mod ϖ (black box)
items.statement: Perfectoid R-algebras are equivalent to perfectoid (R⁺/ϖ)^a-algebras via S ↦ (S°/ϖ)^a (Sch12 states this over a perfectoid field K; ECD applies it over the perfectoid Tate ring R of a totally disconnected X).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 9.3, p. 44, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence (general-base form Perf_R ≃ (R°a/ϖ)-Perf). Scope issue already recorded as PerfectoidSpaces/E8.

items.name: [Sch12, Proposition 7.13]: almost acyclicity of O⁺/ϖ on the affinoid étale site (black box)
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid space X, Y ↦ (O⁺_Y(Y)/ϖ)^a is a sheaf of almost O⁺_X(X)/ϖ-modules on X_ét^aff with vanishing higher cohomology; hence H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is almost zero for i > 0 and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 8.5 (iii), p. 42, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity (ECD Theorem 6.3).

items.name: [Sch12, proof of Proposition 6.18]: plus rings of fibre products mod ϖ (black box)
items.statement: If Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) is a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces and Y ×_X Y = Spa(T, T⁺), then S⁺/ϖ ⊗_{R⁺/ϖ} S⁺/ϖ → T⁺/ϖ is an almost isomorphism.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 8.7, p. 43, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (plus ring of a completed tensor product is almost the completed tensor product of plus rings).

items.name: [KL15, Proposition 8.2.20] after [dJvdP96, Proposition 3.2.2]: reduction to rational and finite étale covers (black box)
items.statement: For an analytic adic space (here a perfectoid space) X, any property P of étale coverings of affinoids that is stable under refinement and composition and holds for rational coverings and for surjective finite étale maps holds for all étale coverings; in particular descent along étale covers reduces to descent along finite étale covers.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 9.7, p. 48, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction both state Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.20; applying them to the perfectoid étale site needs the affinoid étale basis of PerfectoidSpaces:P3.

items.name: [Gro68, after Lemma 11.2]: fppf covers of strictly henselian local rings (black box)
items.statement: Any finitely presented faithfully flat cover of the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring is refined by a finite flat locally free cover.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 9.5, pp. 46–47, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: No atlas node states it (search for 'strictly henselian', 'Gro68', 'EGA IV 17.16'); the D3 stage requires a proof of Lemma 9.5 but does not name this input. Mathlib has HenselianLocalRing but not strict henselization or this refinement statement. Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (strictly henselian local rings of adic spaces), which does not contain it.

items.name: Raynaud–Gruson: flat finite type algebras over a valuation ring are finitely presented (implicit black box)
items.statement: If V is a valuation ring (here C⁺, possibly of higher rank) and A is a flat V-algebra (or ϖ-adically: flat topologically) of finite type, then A is of finite presentation.
items.locator: Used implicitly in the proof of Lemma 9.5, p. 46 ('flat and topologically of finite type (thus, of finite presentation)'), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Not in Mathlib; no atlas node states it. Nearest: AdicSpacesPartII:R2 (formal models over rank-1 O_K, Raynaud–Gruson flattening material), which does not cover higher-rank valuation rings. The paper also asserts without comment that Spf O⁺(V) is topologically of finite type over C⁺.

items.name: Lifting points of the special fibre (implicit black box)
items.statement: For C algebraically closed and 𝔛 a flat formal scheme topologically of finite presentation over O_C, the reduction map 𝔛(O_C) → 𝔛(k) to points over the residue field k is surjective.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 9.5, p. 47 ('the reduction map X(O_C) → X(K) is surjective'), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Planned by node AdicSpacesPartII:R2/specialisation-map (iii): 'for X admissible over O_K, λ maps each classical point … to a closed point of X_s, and every closed point of X_s is the image of a classical point (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 3.4, 3.5)'. With K = C algebraically closed (complete, rank one), classical points are C-points, i.e. O_C-points of 𝔛, and closed points of the special fibre are k-points; a flat formal scheme topologically of finite presentation is admissible. Not in Mathlib. (Marked missing by the extraction; corrected by the review.)

items.name: Definition 11.1: diamond
items.statement: Work in Perf ⊂ Perfd, the perfectoid spaces of characteristic p. A diamond is a sheaf Y for the pro-étale topology on Perf such that Y ≅ X/R, where X is representable by a perfectoid space and R ⊂ X × X is a representable equivalence relation whose projections s, t : R → X are pro-étale. (In particular every diamond is a small sheaf.)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond (statement verbatim, incl. the characteristic-p setting). Uses Perf, the pro-étale topology (D2) and pro-étale morphisms (PerfectoidSpaces:P6).

items.name: Definition 11.2: pro-étale equivalence relation
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space. A pro-étale equivalence relation on X is a representable equivalence relation R ⊂ X × X such that the projections s, t : R → X are pro-étale. No representability of the diagonal of X/R is assumed.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond (defines both 11.1 and 11.2).

items.name: Proposition 11.3(i): X/R is a diamond
items.statement: Let X ∈ Perf and R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation. Then the quotient pro-étale sheaf Y = X/R is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds. The source says the proof is 'clear by definition'.

items.name: Proposition 11.3(ii): effectivity of the relation
items.statement: Let X ∈ Perf, R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation and Y = X/R. Then the natural map R → X ×_Y X of sheaves on Perf is an isomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds; abstract groupoid form in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/groupoid-quotients-and-two-fibre-products.

items.name: Proposition 11.3(iii): refinement of the atlas
items.statement: Let X ∈ Perf, R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation, Y = X/R. Let X̃ → X be a pro-étale cover by a perfectoid space X̃ and R̃ = R ×_{X×X} (X̃ × X̃) ⊂ X̃ × X̃ the induced equivalence relation. Then R̃ is a pro-étale equivalence relation on X̃, and the natural map Ỹ := X̃/R̃ → Y = X/R is an isomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds.

items.name: Proposition 11.3(iv): the atlas map is quasi-pro-étale
items.statement: Let X ∈ Perf, R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation, Y = X/R. Then the map X → Y is quasi-pro-étale (Definition 10.1(i): for every strictly totally disconnected X′ with a map X′ → Y, X′ ×_Y X is representable and pro-étale over X′; local separatedness is part of the definition by Convention 10.2).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds (last clause). Proof uses effective descent of separated pro-étale spaces over a strictly totally disconnected base (ECD Proposition 9.6, node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-separated-pro-etale).

items.name: Proposition 11.4: products and fibre products of diamonds
items.statement: Products and fibre products exist in the category of diamonds: for diamonds Y₁ → Y₃ ← Y₂ the fibre product Y₁ ×_{Y₃} Y₂ (as pro-étale sheaves) is a diamond, and the product Y₁ × Y₂ of two diamonds is a diamond.
items.note: Stage D4 text ('products, fibre products'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds (acceptance clause cites Proposition 11.4). Uses that diagonals of representable maps are pro-étale (Remark 7.9, node PerfectoidSpaces:P6/diagonals-are-pro-etale). A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Products of perfectoid spaces in characteristic p (used in the proof of Proposition 11.4)
items.statement: The product (in Perf) of two perfectoid spaces of characteristic p is again a perfectoid space; locally one reduces to maps to Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), and the product of two copies of Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) is the perfectoid punctured open unit disc over Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/products-in-perf (states existence of absolute products in Perf with affinoid charts and records this example). The source only sketches the reduction.

items.name: Proposition 11.5: characterisation of diamonds by a quasi-pro-étale atlas
items.statement: Let Y be a pro-étale sheaf on Perf. Then Y is a diamond if and only if there is a surjective quasi-pro-étale morphism X → Y from a perfectoid space X. If X (with such a map) is a disjoint union of strictly totally disconnected spaces, then R = X ×_Y X ⊂ X × X is a pro-étale equivalence relation with Y = X/R.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/atlas-characterisation-of-diamonds. The 'only if' direction is Proposition 11.3(iv).

items.name: Proposition 11.6: quasi-pro-étale quotients of diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a pro-étale sheaf on Perf and assume there is a surjective quasi-pro-étale map Y′ → Y where Y′ is a diamond. Then Y is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/atlas-characterisation-of-diamonds (first consequence).

items.name: Proposition 11.7: quasi-pro-étale over a diamond is a diamond
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a quasi-pro-étale map of pro-étale sheaves on Perf, and assume that Y is a diamond. Then Y′ is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/atlas-characterisation-of-diamonds (second consequence).

items.name: Proposition 11.8: quotients of diamonds by quasi-pro-étale equivalence relations
items.statement: Let X be a diamond and R ⊂ X × X an equivalence relation (R only assumed a pro-étale sheaf) such that s, t : R → X are quasi-pro-étale. Then the quotient Y = X/R is a diamond. (R is then automatically a diamond, by Proposition 11.7.)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/atlas-characterisation-of-diamonds (third consequence); proof uses the v-local criterion ECD Proposition 10.11(v).

items.name: Proposition 11.9: diamonds are v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. Then Y is a sheaf for the v-topology on Perf.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves (the node's hypotheses attribute the argument to Fargues; the source says it follows Gabber's argument [Sta, Tag 0APL]). Uses ECD 11.3(iii),(iv), Proposition 9.6 and subcanonicity of the v-topology.

items.name: Proposition 11.10: sub-v-sheaves of diamonds are diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be an injection of v-sheaves, where Y is a diamond. Then Y′ is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves (injection clause); uses ind-representability of sub-v-sheaves of totally disconnected spaces (ECD 10.5, node DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/sub-v-sheaves-of-totally-disconnected-spaces).

items.name: Lemma 11.11: isomorphism criterion on geometric points
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a qcqs map of diamonds. Then f is an isomorphism if and only if for every algebraically closed perfectoid field K with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, the map f(K, K⁺) : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is a bijection.
items.note: Stage D4 ('qcqs geometric-point isomorphism criterion'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves. Reduces to ECD Lemma 5.4 for qcqs perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4).

items.name: Example 11.12 (profinite case): S × Spa(K, O_K) is affinoid perfectoid
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic p and S = lim_i S_i a profinite set (S_i finite), with S the v-sheaf X ↦ C⁰(|X|, S). Then S × Spa(K, O_K) = lim_i (S_i × Spa(K, O_K)) is an affinoid perfectoid space, namely S × Spa(K, O_K) = Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K)).
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds (first proof step) and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set (X × S for affinoid X, property (d) is exactly this formula).

items.name: Example 11.12: compact Hausdorff spaces embed fully faithfully into diamonds
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid field K of characteristic p. For a compact Hausdorff space T let T be the functor X ↦ C⁰(|X|, T) on Perf. Then T ↦ T × Spa(K, O_K) is a fully faithful functor from compact Hausdorff spaces to diamonds over Spa(K, O_K): for a surjection S → T from a profinite set S with R = S ×_T S, one has T × Spa(K, O_K) = (S × Spa(K, O_K))/(R × Spa(K, O_K)), and C⁰(T₁, T₂) → Hom_{Spa(K,O_K)}(T₁ × Spa(K, O_K), T₂ × Spa(K, O_K)) is bijective for all compact Hausdorff T₁, T₂.
items.note: Stage D4 tests name 'the compact-Hausdorff diamond example of 11.12'; node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds (whose proofSteps repeat the false affinoid claim recorded under sourceIssues). Inputs: Stone–Čech surjection and quotient-map property (external items below).

items.name: Proposition 11.13(a): points of a diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond with presentation Y = X/R (X perfectoid, R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation). Let |Y| = {Spa(K, K⁺) → Y}/∼, where (K, K⁺) runs over perfectoid fields K with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺, and Spa(K_i, K_i⁺) → Y (i = 1, 2) are equivalent if there are (K₃, K₃⁺) and surjective maps Spa(K₃, K₃⁺) → Spa(K_i, K_i⁺) making the two composites to Y agree. Then ∼ is an equivalence relation and there is a canonical bijection |X|/|R| ≅ |Y|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space.

items.name: Proposition 11.13(b): independence of the topology
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 11.13, the quotient topology on |Y| induced by the surjection |X| → |Y| is independent of the choice of presentation Y = X/R.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space; proof uses ECD Lemma 2.5 (node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient).

items.name: Definition 11.14: underlying topological space of a diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond, Y = X/R with X perfectoid and R ⊂ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation. The underlying topological space |Y| of Y is the quotient space |X|/|R| (independent of the presentation by Proposition 11.13, and functorial in Y).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space (API Perf.Diamond.space). A wording slip in the printed definition is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 11.15(a): open subfunctors of diamonds are diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. Any open subfunctor of Y is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space.

items.name: Proposition 11.15(b): open subfunctors correspond to open subsets of |Y|
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. There is a bijection between open immersions U ⊂ Y and open subsets V ⊂ |Y|, sending U to V = |U|, and V to the subfunctor U ⊂ Y of those maps X → Y (X perfectoid) for which |X| → |Y| factors over V.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space (API Perf.Diamond.openSubfunctorEquiv). A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 11.15(c): v-surjections induce quotient maps
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is a map of diamonds which is a surjection of v-sheaves, then |f| : |Y′| → |Y| is a quotient map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space (API Perf.Diamond.isQuotientMap_of_surjective); proof uses that open subsheaves form a v-stack (ECD 10.11(i)).

items.name: Example 11.16: |Y| for perfectoid spaces and compact Hausdorff diamonds
items.statement: If Y is a perfectoid space, then |Y| (Definition 11.14) is the usual underlying topological space of Y. If T is a compact Hausdorff space and K a perfectoid field (of characteristic p, as in Example 11.12), then |T × Spa(K, O_K)| = T; in particular |Y| can be far from spectral.
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds (acceptance) and DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space (API Perf.Diamond.space_of_perfectoid).

items.name: Definition 11.17: spatial and locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: A diamond Y is spatial if Y is quasicompact and quasiseparated and |Y| admits a basis of open subsets given by |U| for quasicompact open immersions U ⊂ Y. Y is locally spatial if Y admits an open cover by spatial diamonds.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond.

items.name: Remark after Definition 11.17: perfectoid spaces are locally spatial
items.statement: Any perfectoid space is a locally spatial diamond, and it is spatial precisely when it is qcqs.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (statement and API Perf.Diamond.isSpatial_of_perfectoid). No proof in the source.

items.name: Proposition 11.18(i): |Y| is spectral
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond. Then the underlying topological space |Y| is spectral.
items.note: Stage D5 ('structural and permanence results of 11.17–11.31'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 2, API Perf.Diamond.IsSpatial.spectralSpace). Uses ECD Lemma 2.7 (T0).

items.name: Proposition 11.18(ii): quasicompact opens of spatial diamonds are spatial
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond. Any quasicompact open subfunctor U ⊂ Y is spatial.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (API Perf.Diamond.IsSpatial.quasicompactOpen).

items.name: Proposition 11.18(iii): |X′| → |Y| is spectral and generalizing
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond. For any perfectoid space X′ with a map X′ → Y, the induced map of locally spectral spaces |X′| → |Y| is spectral and generalizing.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 2). Uses ECD Lemma 2.9 (node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/spectral-quotient-criterion).

items.name: Proposition 11.19(i): |Y| locally spectral
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Then |Y| is locally spectral.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 3). Source proof: 'Left as an exercise to the reader' (recorded by the packet's gaps list).

items.name: Proposition 11.19(ii): open subfunctors of locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Any open subfunctor U ⊂ Y is locally spatial.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 3); proof left to the reader in the source.

items.name: Proposition 11.19(iii): qc/qs detected on |Y|
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Then Y is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated) if and only if |Y| is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (API Perf.Diamond.IsLocallySpatial.qcqs_iff); proof left to the reader in the source.

items.name: Proposition 11.19(iv): maps of locally spatial diamonds are spectral and generalizing
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. For any locally spatial diamond Y′ with a map Y′ → Y, the induced map of locally spectral spaces |Y′| → |Y| is spectral and generalizing.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (API Perf.Diamond.IsLocallySpatial.isSpectralMap); proof left to the reader in the source.

items.name: Proposition 11.19 (final statement): generalizations are totally ordered
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. For any y ∈ |Y|, the set of generalizations of y is totally ordered.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (API Perf.Diamond.IsLocallySpatial.generalizations_totallyOrdered); proof: choose a surjection from a perfectoid space and use (iv).

items.name: Proposition 11.20: quasicompact injections into locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a quasicompact injection of v-sheaves, where Y is a locally spatial diamond. Then Y′ is a locally spatial diamond, |Y′| ⊂ |Y| is a pro-constructible and generalizing subset carrying the subspace topology, and the map Y′ → Y ×_{|Y|} |Y′| of v-sheaves is an isomorphism (T denoting the v-sheaf X ↦ C⁰(|X|, T)).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/injection-and-finite-etale-permanence. Uses ECD Corollary 10.6 and Lemma 2.5.

items.name: Lemma 11.21: finite étale over (locally) spatial is (locally) spatial
items.statement: Let Y be a (locally) spatial diamond and Y′ → Y a finite étale map of pro-étale sheaves. Then Y′ is a (locally) spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/injection-and-finite-etale-permanence (the 'tree' argument). A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: κ-small diamonds (after Lemma 11.22)
items.statement: For κ a cutoff cardinal as in Lemma 4.1, a diamond is κ-small if it admits a surjection from a κ-small perfectoid space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons (κ-smallness clause; the definition itself is not stated in any node, but is presupposed by the κ-small clauses of that node and of DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation); κ-small perfectoid spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space.

items.name: Lemma 11.22(a): cofiltered limits of diamonds
items.statement: Let Y_i, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of diamonds with qcqs transition maps. Then Y = lim_i Y_i is a diamond, there is a bijective continuous map |Y| → lim_i |Y_i|, and the maps Y → Y_i are qcqs.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons. Proof reduces to ordinal-indexed systems (external item below) and uses ECD Lemma 7.19 and Proposition 11.10.

items.name: Lemma 11.22(b): limits of (locally) spatial diamonds
items.statement: In Lemma 11.22, if all Y_i are (locally) spatial, then Y is (locally) spatial and |Y| → lim_i |Y_i| is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons; uses ECD Lemma 2.11 (node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

items.name: Lemma 11.22(c): size bound
items.statement: In Lemma 11.22, if κ is as in Lemma 4.1, I is κ-small and all Y_i are κ′-small for some κ′ < κ, then Y is κ-small.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons (uses Lemma 4.1(iii), node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal).

items.name: Proposition 11.23(i),(iii): finite étale and qc separated étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Y_i, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of qcqs diamonds with limit Y = lim_i Y_i. (i) The base change functors (Y_i)_fét → Y_fét induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (Y_i)_fét → Y_fét, where Y_fét is the category of finite étale diamonds over Y. (iii) With Y_ét,qc,sep ⊂ Y_ét,qcqs the full subcategory of quasicompact separated étale diamonds over Y, the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (Y_i)_ét,qc,sep → Y_ét,qc,sep.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons; (i) and (iii) are proved simultaneously via v-descent (ECD 10.11) and ECD Proposition 6.4 (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/P6).

items.name: Proposition 11.23(ii): qcqs étale objects over a limit
items.statement: Let Y_i be a cofiltered inverse system of qcqs diamonds with limit Y, and Y_ét,qcqs the category of (locally separated) étale qcqs diamonds over Y. Then the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (Y_i)_ét,qcqs → Y_ét,qcqs.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons (last proof step: cover by qc separated opens and descend gluing data).

items.name: Proposition 11.24(a): universally open strictly totally disconnected presentation
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond. Then there is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a surjective and universally open quasi-pro-étale map f : X → Y that can be written as a cofiltered inverse limit of étale maps which are composites of quasicompact open immersions and finite étale maps. If κ is as in Lemma 4.1 and Y is κ-small, X can be taken κ-small.
items.note: Stage D5 ('the universally open strictly totally disconnected presentation and its converse'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation.

items.name: Proposition 11.24(b): converse
items.statement: Let Y be a qcqs diamond admitting a surjective and universally open quasi-pro-étale map X → Y from a perfectoid space X. Then Y is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation; proof uses ECD Lemma 2.10 (node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/spectral-quotient-criterion) and Lemma 7.18.

items.name: Remark 11.25: converse with a (locally) spatial source
items.statement: If Y is a qcqs diamond admitting a surjective and universally open quasi-pro-étale map Y′ → Y, where Y′ is a (locally) spatial diamond, then Y is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence (last sentence of statement) and DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation.

items.name: Proposition 11.26: spatial diamonds with split covers are strictly totally disconnected
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond such that every surjective étale map Ỹ → Y that can be written as a composite of quasicompact open immersions and finite étale maps splits. Then Y is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation (statement: 'rests on the fact that ...'). Uses Fargues' Lemma 7.2 (node DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/split-cover-characterisation). An error and a misprint in the proof are recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Lemma 11.27: spatial diamonds with affinoid perfectoid components
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond such that every connected component of Y is representable by an affinoid perfectoid space. Then Y is representable by an affinoid perfectoid space (namely Spa(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) = eq((B, B⁺) ⇉ (C, C⁺)) for a presentation Y = X/R, X = Spa(B, B⁺) strictly totally disconnected, R = Spa(C, C⁺) affinoid pro-étale).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/universally-open-presentation (statement: 'a spatial diamond all of whose connected components are affinoid perfectoid spaces is an affinoid perfectoid space'); related node PerfectoidSpaces:P8/perfectoid-from-perfectoid-components applies it. Uses almost vanishing of H¹_v(O⁺) (ECD 8.8) and the almost-mathematics equivalence (external item below).

items.name: Corollary 11.28: quasi-pro-étale over locally spatial is locally spatial
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and Y′ → Y a quasi-pro-étale map of pro-étale sheaves (locally separated by Convention 10.2). Then Y′ is a locally spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence.

items.name: Corollary 11.29: fibre products of (locally) spatial diamonds
items.statement: A fibre product of (locally) spatial diamonds is (locally) spatial.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence. A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 11.30(a): 2-out-of-3 for quasi-pro-étale maps
items.statement: Let f : Y₁ → Y₂ and g : Y₂ → Y₃ be maps of locally spatial diamonds with composite h = g ∘ f. Assume that f is quasi-pro-étale and surjective, h is quasi-pro-étale, and g is separated. Then g is quasi-pro-étale.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/two-out-of-three-for-quasi-pro-etale (whose proofSteps repeat the |f| misprint). Misprints in the proof are recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 11.30(b): 2-out-of-3 for étale and finite étale maps
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 11.30 (f quasi-pro-étale surjective, h quasi-pro-étale, g separated, all locally spatial diamonds), if f and h are in addition étale (resp. finite étale), then g is étale (resp. finite étale).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/two-out-of-three-for-quasi-pro-etale (last proof step).

items.name: Lemma 11.31: local structure of étale maps of locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be an étale map (locally separated, Convention 10.2) of locally spatial diamonds. Then for every y′ ∈ |Y′| with image y ∈ |Y| there are open neighbourhoods V′ ⊂ Y′ of y′ and V ⊃ f(V′) of y such that f|_{V′} : V′ → V factors as a quasicompact open immersion V′ ↪ W followed by a finite étale map W → V.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/local-structure-of-etale-maps (whose proofSteps repeat 'the open point', see sourceIssues). Uses ECD Lemma 9.9 and Proposition 11.23.

items.name: Definition 12.1: small v-sheaf
items.statement: A small v-sheaf is a v-sheaf Y on Perf such that there is a surjective map of v-sheaves X → Y for some perfectoid space X.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Remark 12.2: sources of small v-sheaves
items.statement: Every diamond is a small v-sheaf. If Y is a v-sheaf admitting a surjective map of v-sheaves X → Y from a diamond X, then Y is a small v-sheaf. Every quasicompact v-sheaf is small.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks (API IsSmallVSheaf.ofDiamond, .ofSurjectionFromDiamond).

items.name: Proposition 12.3(a): small v-sheaves are quotients of diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-sheaf and X → Y a surjective map of v-sheaves, where X is a diamond. Then R = X ×_Y X is a diamond, and Y = X/R as v-sheaves.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks (proof step 3). Uses Propositions 11.4 and 11.10.

items.name: Proposition 12.3(b): locally spatial relation for quasiseparated Y
items.statement: If Y is a quasiseparated small v-sheaf and X → Y is a surjective map of v-sheaves with X a locally spatial diamond, then R = X ×_Y X is a locally spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks (API IsSmallVSheaf.relation_locallySpatial). Uses Proposition 11.20 and Corollary 11.29.

items.name: Proposition 12.3(c): spatial relation for qcqs Y
items.statement: If Y is a qcqs v-sheaf and X → Y is a surjective map of v-sheaves with X a spatial diamond, then R = X ×_Y X is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Definition 12.4: small v-stack
items.statement: A small v-stack is a v-stack Y on Perf such that there is a surjective map of v-stacks X → Y from a perfectoid space X for which R = X ×_Y X is a small v-sheaf.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks (API Perf.IsSmallVStack). 2-fibre products and stack quotients from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/groupoid-quotients-and-two-fibre-products.

items.name: Remark after Definition 12.4: qcqs v-stacks are small
items.statement: All qcqs v-stacks are small v-stacks.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks (statement: 'every qcqs v-stack is small'; API IsSmallVStack.ofQuasicompact). Source: 'arguing as in Remark 12.2'.

items.name: Lemma 12.5: isomorphism criterion for v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a qcqs map of v-stacks (quasiseparated in the sense of Convention 8.4, cf. Remark 12.6). Then f is an isomorphism if and only if for all algebraically closed perfectoid fields K with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, the functor f(K, K⁺) : Y′(K, K⁺) → Y(K, K⁺) is an equivalence of groupoids.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks. A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Proposition 12.7(a): points of a small v-stack
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack with a presentation Y = X/R as a quotient of a diamond X by a small v-sheaf R → X × X, and let R̃ → R be a surjection from a diamond. There is a canonical bijection between |X|/|R̃| and |Y| = {Spa(K, K⁺) → Y}/∼, with (K, K⁺) and ∼ as in Proposition 11.13.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks. Source proof: 'The proof of Proposition 11.13 carries over'.

items.name: Proposition 12.7(b): independence of the topology for small v-stacks
items.statement: In Proposition 12.7, the quotient topology on |Y| induced by the surjection |X| → |Y| is independent of the choice of presentation Y = X/R.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Definition 12.8: underlying space of a small v-stack
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack with presentation Y = X/R (X a diamond, R → X × X a small v-sheaf) and R̃ → R a surjection from a diamond. The underlying topological space of Y is |Y| := |X|/|R̃| (equivalently |X|/|R| after defining |·| for small v-sheaves first, since |R̃| → |R| is surjective).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks (the node's hypotheses record the two-step description).

items.name: Proposition 12.9(a): open sub-v-stacks are small
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack. Any open sub-v-stack of Y is a small v-stack.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks. Source proof: the arguments of Proposition 11.15 apply.

items.name: Proposition 12.9(b): open sub-v-stacks ↔ open subsets of |Y|
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack. There is a bijection between open sub-v-stacks U ⊂ Y and open subsets V ⊂ |Y|, sending U to |U| and V to the subfunctor of those maps X → Y for which |X| → |Y| factors over V.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Proposition 12.9(c): surjections give quotient maps
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is a surjective map of small v-stacks, then |f| : |Y′| → |Y| is a quotient map.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Proposition 12.10(a): fibre products of small v-stacks
items.statement: Let Y₁ → Y₃ ← Y₂ be a diagram of small v-stacks. Then Y = Y₁ ×_{Y₃} Y₂ is a small v-stack.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks (API IsSmallVStack.fibreProduct in the sibling node). No proof in the source beyond 'follows from the similar result for perfectoid spaces'.

items.name: Proposition 12.10(b): points of a fibre product
items.statement: For small v-stacks Y₁ → Y₃ ← Y₂ and Y = Y₁ ×_{Y₃} Y₂, the map |Y| → |Y₁| ×_{|Y₃|} |Y₂| is surjective.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Lemma 12.11(a): surjections are surjective on points
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-stacks. If f is a surjective map of v-stacks, then |f| : |Y′| → |Y| is surjective.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Lemma 12.11(b): quasicompact + surjective on points ⇒ v-surjective
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-stacks. If f is quasicompact and |f| : |Y′| → |Y| is surjective, then f is a surjective map of v-stacks.
items.note: Stage D4 ('The converse implication requires the stated qc hypothesis'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/spaces-and-surjectivity-for-small-v-stacks.

items.name: Definition 12.12: spatial and locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: A v-sheaf Y is spatial if it is qcqs (in particular small) and |Y| has a basis for the topology given by |U| for quasicompact open subfunctors U ⊂ Y. Y is locally spatial if it is small and has an open cover by spatial v-sheaves.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (v-sheaf clause, API Perf.VSheaf.IsSpatial).

items.name: Proposition 12.13(i): spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf. Then |Y| is a spectral space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4: 'the same statements hold verbatim for spatial v-sheaves'). Packet coverage note assigns 12.12–12.17 to D5. Source proof: identical to 11.18, writing Y = X/R with X, R spatial diamonds.

items.name: Proposition 12.13(ii): spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf. Any quasicompact open subfunctor U ⊂ Y is spatial.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4: 'the same statements hold verbatim for spatial v-sheaves'). Packet coverage note assigns 12.12–12.17 to D5. Source proof: identical to 11.18, writing Y = X/R with X, R spatial diamonds.

items.name: Proposition 12.13(iii): spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf. For any perfectoid space X′ with a map X′ → Y, the induced map of locally spectral spaces |X′| → |Y| is spectral and generalizing.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4: 'the same statements hold verbatim for spatial v-sheaves'). Packet coverage note assigns 12.12–12.17 to D5. Source proof: identical to 11.18, writing Y = X/R with X, R spatial diamonds.

items.name: Proposition 12.14(i): locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial v-sheaf. Then |Y| is locally spectral.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4). The source gives no proof at all (only □); the diamond analogue 11.19 is itself left to the reader.

items.name: Proposition 12.14(ii): locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial v-sheaf. Any open subfunctor U ⊂ Y is locally spatial.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4). The source gives no proof at all (only □); the diamond analogue 11.19 is itself left to the reader.

items.name: Proposition 12.14(iii): locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial v-sheaf. Then Y is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated) if and only if |Y| is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4). The source gives no proof at all (only □); the diamond analogue 11.19 is itself left to the reader.

items.name: Proposition 12.14(iv): locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial v-sheaf. For any locally spatial v-sheaf Y′ with a map Y′ → Y, the induced map of locally spectral spaces |Y′| → |Y| is spectral and generalizing.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4). The source gives no proof at all (only □); the diamond analogue 11.19 is itself left to the reader.

items.name: Proposition 12.14 (final statement): locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial v-sheaf. For y ∈ |Y|, the set of generalizations of y is totally ordered.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-diamond (proof step 4). The source gives no proof at all (only □); the diamond analogue 11.19 is itself left to the reader.

items.name: Proposition 12.15: characterisations of injections of small v-sheaves
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-sheaves, and assume that f is qcqs, or that Y′ and Y are locally spatial. The following are equivalent: (i) f is an injective map of v-sheaves; (ii) for all perfectoid fields K with open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, f(K, K⁺) : Y′(K, K⁺) → Y(K, K⁺) is injective; (iii) |f| : |Y′| → |Y| is injective and f is final in the category of maps g : Z → Y from small v-sheaves Z for which |g| : |Z| → |Y| factors over a continuous map |Z| → |Y′|; equivalently Y′ = Y ×_{|Y|} |Y′|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks (second half of statement). Analogue of ECD Proposition 5.3 (PerfectoidSpaces:P4).

items.name: Lemma 12.16: finite étale over spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf and Y′ → Y a finite étale map of v-sheaves. Then Y′ is a spatial v-sheaf.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/injection-and-finite-etale-permanence (v-sheaf clause).

items.name: Lemma 12.17(a): cofiltered limits of small v-sheaves
items.statement: Let Y_i, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of small v-sheaves with qcqs transition maps. Then Y = lim_i Y_i is a small v-sheaf, the maps Y → Y_i are qcqs, and the continuous map |Y| → lim_i |Y_i| is bijective.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons ('The same statements hold for small v-sheaves'). A misprint in the proof is recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Lemma 12.17(b): limits of locally spatial v-sheaves
items.statement: In Lemma 12.17, if all Y_i are locally spatial, then Y is locally spatial and |Y| → lim_i |Y_i| is a homeomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons.

items.name: Lemma 12.17(c): size bound for small v-sheaves
items.statement: In Lemma 12.17, if κ is as in Lemma 4.1, I is κ-small and all Y_i are κ′-small for some κ′ < κ, then Y is κ-small.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons.

items.name: Lemma 12.17(d): finite étale and qc separated étale objects over limits of qcqs v-sheaves
items.statement: In Lemma 12.17, if all Y_i are qcqs, then Y is qcqs and the base change functors induce equivalences 2-colim_i (Y_i)_fét → Y_fét and 2-colim_i (Y_i)_ét,qc,sep → Y_ét,qc,sep.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons; proved simultaneously via v-descent (ECD 10.11) and Proposition 11.23.

items.name: Lemma 12.17(e): qcqs étale objects over limits of qcqs v-sheaves
items.statement: In Lemma 12.17, if all Y_i are qcqs, the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim_i (Y_i)_ét,qcqs → Y_ét,qcqs (étale maps being locally separated by Convention 10.2).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons.

items.name: Theorem 12.18: spatial v-sheaf criterion for diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf such that there exists a perfectoid space X with a quasi-pro-étale map f : X → Y for which |f| : |X| → |Y| is surjective. Then Y is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Stage D5 ('spatial v-sheaf criterion of 12.18–12.21'); node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-v-sheaf-criterion.

items.name: Remark 12.19: the hypothesis of Theorem 12.18 is a condition on points
items.statement: The hypothesis of Theorem 12.18 is equivalent to: for every y ∈ |Y| there is a quasi-pro-étale map Spa(C, C⁺) → Y with y in its image, C an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field and C⁺ ⊂ C an open and bounded valuation subring (take the disjoint union of all such maps, which is not quasicompact, so Lemma 12.11 does not apply). This is much weaker than f being surjective.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-v-sheaf-criterion (statement).

items.name: Proposition 12.20: spatial v-sheaves with split covers
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf such that there exists a quasi-pro-étale map f : X → Y from a perfectoid space X with |f| : |X| → |Y| surjective. Assume that every surjective étale map Ỹ → Y that can be written as a composite of quasicompact open immersions and finite étale maps splits. Then Y is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-v-sheaf-criterion. The proof repeats that of 11.26, including the error recorded under sourceIssues.

items.name: Lemma 12.21: spatial v-sheaves with affinoid perfectoid components
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial v-sheaf such that every connected component of Y is representable by an affinoid perfectoid space. Then Y is representable by an affinoid perfectoid space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/spatial-v-sheaf-criterion. The proof applies Lemma 11.27 to the relation R without checking its hypothesis that the components of R are affinoid perfectoid (true: they are components of X_c ×_{Y_c} X_c, X_c = X ×_{π₀(Y)} {c}, a routine check).

items.name: External: Stone–Čech profinite cover of a compact Hausdorff space
items.statement: Every compact Hausdorff space T admits a continuous surjection S → T from a profinite set S, e.g. S the Stone–Čech compactification of T regarded as a discrete set; then R = S ×_T S ⊂ S × S is closed, hence profinite.
items.note: Mathlib: CompHaus.projectivePresentation is the map Ultrafilter T → T (Stone–Čech compactification of T as a discrete set) with epi field proved by surjectivity; CompHaus.epi_iff_surjective; Ultrafilter T is compact T2 and totally disconnected (unnamed TotallyDisconnectedSpace instance in Mathlib/Topology/Compactification/StoneCech.lean), hence profinite. Also planned as DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/profinite-presentation-of-compact-hausdorff.

items.name: External: surjections of compact Hausdorff spaces are quotient maps
items.statement: Any continuous surjection f : T₁ → T₂ from a quasicompact space to a compact Hausdorff space (in particular any surjective map of compact Hausdorff spaces) is a quotient map.
items.note: Mathlib Topology.IsQuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous ([CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y], surjective continuous f ⇒ IsQuotientMap f), read in Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff.lean:682; it is exactly the classical statement used.

items.name: External: perfectoid A-algebras ≃ perfectoid (A⁺/ϖ)ᵃ-algebras
items.statement: For a perfectoid Tate ring A with ring of integral elements A⁺ and pseudouniformizer ϖ (with ϖ^p | p), reduction S ↦ (S⁺/ϖ)ᵃ gives an equivalence between perfectoid A-algebras and perfectoid (A⁺/ϖ)ᵃ-algebras (Scholze 2012 §5, over a general perfectoid base).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence (Perf_R ≃ R°a-Perf ≃ (R°a/ϖ)-Perf over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring); A⁺ᵃ = A°ᵃ since A°° · A° ⊂ A⁺. Used to show that (A⁺/ϖ)ᵃ = eq((B⁺/ϖ)ᵃ ⇉ (C⁺/ϖ)ᵃ) commutes with passage to connected components.

items.name: External: reduction of cofiltered limits to ordinal-indexed limits
items.statement: The limit of a cofiltered inverse system (with qcqs transition maps) may be computed as a transfinite limit over the ordinals µ < λ of some ordinal λ ('we can assume that I is the category of ordinals µ < λ').
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 11.22, Proposition 11.23 and Lemma 12.17, pp. 63–64, 74, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Mathlib has only the first step, a final functor from a directed poset (CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.exists_directed, Stacks 0032; dual for cofiltered). The passage from a directed poset to a well-ordered transfinite chain is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti, and the DiamondsAndVStacks packet uses it only as an unexplained proof step of D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons.

items.name: Definition 13.1: maps of v-stacks representable in diamonds
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is representable in diamonds if for all diamonds X with a map X → Y, the fibre product Y′ ×_Y X is a diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability states this definition verbatim. D5 description: 'Construct representability in diamonds and in locally spatial diamonds, including the different pro-étale and v-locality assumptions in §13 … The source index assigns §13 here'. All notions of §13 are examples of 0-truncated maps.

items.name: Proposition 13.2(i): over a diamond, representable in diamonds ⇔ source is a diamond
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks. If Y is a diamond, then f is representable in diamonds if and only if Y′ is a diamond.
items.note: Proof: Proposition 11.4 (fibre products of diamonds exist). Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability; stated in the node's acceptance ('For Y a diamond, f is representable in diamonds exactly when Y' is a diamond') and test diamond_base; also covered by D5 description: 'Construct representability in diamonds and in locally spatial diamonds, including the different pro-étale and v-locality assumptions in §13 … The source index assigns §13 here'.

items.name: Proposition 13.2(ii): representability in diamonds is stable under pullback
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be maps of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is representable in diamonds, then f̃ is representable in diamonds.
items.note: Clear from the definition. Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability.

items.name: Proposition 13.2(iii): representability in diamonds descends along pro-étale surjections
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be maps of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If Ỹ → Y is surjective as a map of pro-étale stacks and f̃ is representable in diamonds, then f is representable in diamonds.
items.note: Proof: reduce to Y a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space via a quasi-pro-étale cover and Proposition 11.6, then lift along a pro-étale cover X̃ → X. Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability ('the different pro-étale and v-locality assumptions in §13').

items.name: Definition 13.3: maps representable in (locally) spatial diamonds; (locally) spatial maps
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is representable in (locally) spatial diamonds if for all (locally) spatial diamonds X with a map X → Y, the fibre product Y′ ×_Y X is a (locally) spatial diamond. If f : Y′ → Y is a map of diamonds which is representable in (locally) spatial diamonds, f is also called a (locally) spatial map of diamonds.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability states this definition.

items.name: Remark after Definition 13.3: spatial = locally spatial + qcqs (for maps)
items.statement: If a map of v-stacks f : Y′ → Y is representable in spatial diamonds, then it is representable in locally spatial diamonds; the converse holds precisely when f is qcqs.
items.note: Stated as 'clear' without proof. Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability states it ('A map is representable in spatial diamonds exactly when it is representable in locally spatial diamonds and qcqs').

items.name: Proposition 13.4(i): locally spatial ⇒ representable in diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks. If f is representable in locally spatial diamonds, then f is representable in diamonds.
