items.name: Proposition 23.4: criteria for Rf^! to be a twisted pullback over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, let f : Y → X be a compactifiable map from a locally spatial diamond Y of locally dim.trg f < ∞, and fix a prime ℓ ≠ p. The following are equivalent. (i) The natural transformation Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ), adjoint to Rf_!(Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^*−) = Rf_!Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} id → id (projection formula 22.23), is an equivalence. (ii) Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is equivalent to a functor A ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^* for some A ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ). (iii) Rf^! commutes with arbitrary direct sums, and for all connected components X₀ = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊂ X with an open subset j : U ⊂ X₀ and pullbacks f_U : V → U, f₀ : Y₀ → X₀, j′ : V → Y₀, the map j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ → Rf₀^! j_! F_ℓ adjoint to Rf₀_! j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! F_ℓ → j_! F_ℓ is an equivalence. (iv) For all affinoid pro-étale maps g : X′ → X with pullback f′ : Y′ → X′, h : Y′ → Y, the natural transformation h^* Rf^! → Rf′^! g^* : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y′, F_ℓ) adjoint to Rf′_! h^* Rf^! = g^* Rf_! Rf^! → g^* is an equivalence, and for all X₀, U, j as in (iii) the natural transformation j′_! Rf_U^! → Rf₀^! j_! : D_ét(U, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y₀, F_ℓ) adjoint to Rf₀_! j′_! Rf_U^! = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! → j_! is an equivalence.
items.note: S4: 'Prove 23.4–23.7, including the equivalences of criteria over strictly totally disconnected bases'. The printed proof uses 23.16(i) (planned in S3 precisely for this reason) and Lemma 23.6. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.4, final assertion: ℓ-power-torsion coefficients
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 23.4, under the equivalent conditions (i)–(iv), for any ℓ-power-torsion ring Λ the natural transformation Rf^!Λ ⊗_Λ f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S4 (23.4). Proof reduces to Λ = Z/ℓ^m Z via Remark 23.2 and uses self-injectivity of Z/ℓ^m Z. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Lemma 23.6: pushforward along a profinite projection
items.statement: Let S be a profinite set, let Y be a small v-sheaf, and consider h : Y × S → Y. Then for any ring Λ and any C ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), one has a natural isomorphism Rh_* h^* C ≃ C⁰(S, Λ) ⊗_Λ C, where C⁰(S, Λ) is the Λ-module of continuous maps S → Λ.
items.note: S4: 'the profinite-projection calculation'. The printed proof uses Definition 22.4 and the projection formula 22.11, valid only for nΛ = 0 with n prime to p (see sourceIssues). C⁰(S, Λ) corresponds to Mathlib's LocallyConstant S Λ, but the lemma itself is not in any library. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.7: Rf^! preserves direct sums iff Rf_! preserves constructibility
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, f : Y → X a compactifiable map from a spatial diamond Y with dim.trg f < ∞, and fix a prime ℓ ≠ p. The functor Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) commutes with arbitrary direct sums if and only if for all constructible sheaves F of F_ℓ-vector spaces on Y_ét and all i ≥ 0, the !-pushforward R^i f_! F is constructible on X_ét.
items.note: S4 ('the compactness/direct-sum criterion'). Inputs: Theorem 22.5, Proposition 20.10 (C9 nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/compact-generators, C9/finite-field-compact-objects) and Neeman's observation [Nee96] (missing, see separate item). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 23.8 (second paragraph): invertible objects of D_ét(Y, F_ℓ)
items.statement: For a locally spatial diamond Y, an object D ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is invertible if it is locally (equivalently, in the v-, quasi-pro-étale, or étale topology of Y) isomorphic to F_ℓ[n] for some integer n ∈ Z.
items.note: S4 ('tensor with an invertible object followed by pullback'). Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves of modules (TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/Invertible) but not this derived étale notion. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 23.8: ℓ-cohomologically smooth morphism
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, and let ℓ ≠ p be a prime. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if f is compactifiable, locally dim.trg f < ∞, and for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a map X → Y and pullback f_X : Y′ ×_Y X → X, the functor Rf_X^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ) is equivalent to a functor of the form D_{f_X} ⊗_{F_ℓ} f_X^* for some invertible object D_{f_X} ∈ D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ). (It is not required a priori that the equivalence be natural or that D_{f_X} commute with base change; these follow from Proposition 23.12.)
items.note: S4: 'Define ℓ-cohomological smoothness exactly as in 23.8'. Printed with f^* for f_X^* (see sourceIssues). Consumers: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps extends it to stacky maps (FS IV.1). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.10: practical criterion for ℓ-cohomological smoothness
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in spatial diamonds, and let ℓ ≠ p be a prime. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if: (i) dim.trg f < ∞; (ii) for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a map g : X → Y and pullback f_X : Y′ ×_Y X → X, and any constructible étale sheaf F of F_ℓ-vector spaces on the spatial diamond Y′ ×_Y X, R^i f_{X!} F is constructible on X for all i ≥ 0; (iii) for any X = Spa(C, C⁺) (C algebraically closed, C⁺ ⊂ C open and bounded valuation subring) with a map to Y and a quasicompact open subset j : U → X, with pullbacks f_U : Y′ ×_Y U → U, f_X, j′ : Y′ ×_Y U → Y′ ×_Y X, the natural map j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ → Rf_X^! j_! F_ℓ adjoint to Rf_{X!} j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! F_ℓ → j_! F_ℓ is an equivalence; (iv) for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid X with a map g : X → Y and pullback f_X, the !-pullback Rf_X^! F_ℓ ∈ D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ) is invertible.
items.note: S4 ('(23.10–23.12)'). Proof from 23.4 ((ii)⇔(iii)) and 23.7. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.11: ℓ-cohomologically smooth maps are universally open
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some ℓ ≠ p. Then f is universally open, i.e. for all X → Y the map |Y′ ×_Y X| → |X| is open.
items.note: S4 ('Prove universal openness'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(i): Rf^! is a twist of pullback; the dualizing complex is invertible
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. The natural transformation Rf^!Λ ⊗_Λ f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ) is an equivalence, and the dualizing complex D_f := Rf^!Λ ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) is invertible, in fact étale locally isomorphic to Λ[n] for some integer n ∈ Z.
items.note: S4: 'Prove that the a priori unspecified equivalence becomes the canonical tensor transformation and that the dualizing object is Rf^!Λ'. Proved jointly with (iii). = Theorem 1.10(i). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(ii): quasicompact smooth Rf_! preserves perfect-constructible complexes
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. If f is quasicompact, then for any perfect-constructible A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ), the proper pushforward Rf_! A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) is perfect-constructible.
items.note: S4: 'preservation of perfect-constructible complexes under quasicompact cohomologically smooth Rf!'. Uses Proposition 20.17 (C9/compact-iff-perfect-constructible). = Theorem 1.11 for Λ = F_ℓ. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(iii): Rf^! commutes with arbitrary base change for smooth f
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. If g : Ỹ → Y is a map of small v-sheaves with base change f̃ : Ỹ′ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′, then the natural transformation g′^* Rf^! → Rf̃^! g^* : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ′, Λ), adjoint to Rf̃_! g′^* Rf^! = g^* Rf_! Rf^! → g^*, is an equivalence. In particular the dualizing complex commutes with base change: g′^* D_f = D_f̃.
items.note: S4 ('base change of the dualizing object'). Proof via a v-hypercover and Proposition 17.3. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.13 (first part): composites of ℓ-cohomologically smooth maps
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be separated morphisms of small v-stacks and ℓ ≠ p a prime. If f and g are representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f ∘ g is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4 ('Prove composition'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.13 (second part): smoothness descends along smooth surjections
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be separated morphisms of small v-stacks and ℓ ≠ p a prime. If g and f ∘ g are representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, g is surjective, and f is representable in diamonds and compactifiable, then f is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4: 'the precise reverse implication of 23.13 ... keep the assumptions that the intermediate map is representable in diamonds and compactifiable, as well as surjectivity'. The paper (p. 150) notes compactifiability of f can be dropped when g has local sections after pullback to strictly totally disconnected spaces (22.3(vii)), e.g. when g is formally smooth ([FS26, Def. IV.3.1, Prop. IV.3.5]). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 23.14: representability in locally spatial diamonds descends along universally open covers
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is a separated 0-truncated map of small v-stacks that is representable in diamonds, and g : Y″ → Y′ is a universally open (e.g. ℓ-cohomologically smooth), separated and surjective map of small v-stacks such that f ∘ g is representable in locally spatial diamonds, then f is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S4 plans 23.13, whose proof contains the smooth case of this argument (via 23.11, Proposition 13.4 and Lemma 2.10); no stage or node states the universally-open generalisation. DiamondsAndVStacks:D5 owns relative representability but does not state it.

items.name: Proposition 23.15 (first part): ℓ-cohomological smoothness is stable under base change
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Let g : Ỹ → Y be a map of small v-stacks with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f̃ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.15 (converse): ℓ-cohomological smoothness is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 23.15, if f̃ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, g is a surjective map of v-stacks, and locally dim.trg f < ∞, then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4: 'Prove target v-descent as in 23.15, retaining local finiteness of dim.trg f as an assumption on f itself' (the paper says it is unclear whether that condition is v-local). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(i): Rg^! commutes with pushforward
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg g < ∞, and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ). Then Rg^! Rf_* A ≅ Rf′_* Rg̃^! A.
items.note: S3: 'prove the formal exceptional base-change identity 23.16(i) by taking right adjoints of 22.19 ... used earlier in the printed proof of 23.4'. = Theorem 1.9(iii). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(ii): smooth base change
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and Λ is ℓ-power torsion. Then for all A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), the base change morphism g^* Rf_* A → Rf′_* g̃^* A is an isomorphism.
items.note: S4 ('Prove smooth base change and the remaining identities of 23.16–23.17'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(iii): Rf^! commutes with smooth base change
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and Λ is ℓ-power torsion [and, implicitly, that f is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, so that Rf^! and Rf′^! are defined]. Then for all A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), the map g̃^* Rf^! A → Rf′^! g^* A adjoint to Rf^! A → Rf^! Rg_* g^* A = Rg̃_* Rf′^! g^* A is an equivalence.
items.note: S4: 'when applying 23.16(iii), provide the hypotheses making the vertical map's exceptional inverse image available, rather than relying on an ill-typed standalone formula' (hypothesis omitted in print; see sourceIssues). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.17: smooth pullback commutes with internal Hom
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth [and Λ ℓ-power torsion, as in Theorem 1.10(ii); omitted in print]. There is a functorial isomorphism f^* RHom(A, B) ≅ RHom(f^* A, f^* B) in A, B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ).
items.note: S4 ('the remaining identities of 23.16–23.17'). Proof: 23.3(ii) and 23.12(i). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: The ball B (Theorem 24.1)
items.statement: B is the v-sheaf on Perf with B(R, R⁺) = R⁺ (the absolute perfectoid closed unit ball), and f : B → * the projection to the point.
items.note: S5: 'Prove Theorem 24.1 for the absolute perfectoid-ball functor B(R,R⁺) = R⁺. After perfectoid base change this is the perfected ball.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 24.1: the ball is ℓ-cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex Λ(1)[2]
items.statement: Let f : B → * be the projection from the ball to the point, where B(R, R⁺) = R⁺. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth for any prime ℓ ≠ p, and for any ring Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p, one has a canonical isomorphism D_f = Rf^!Λ ≅ Λ(1)[2].
items.note: S5: 'Use H3's curve trace/duality and H4's relative constructibility input to obtain the canonical normalization Rf^!Λ ≃ Λ(1)[2]'. Classical inputs: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/relative-ball-compact-support, H3/curve-trace, H3/curve-poincare-duality, H3/duality-open-extension-compatibility, H3/lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension; H4 (Hub96 6.2.2, stage only). The printed proof treats Λ = F_ℓ; the passage to general Λ with nΛ = 0 is not written out. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.2: quotients by free profinite actions of pro-order prime to ℓ
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some prime ℓ ≠ p. Assume that there is a profinite group K of pro-order prime to ℓ with a free action K × Y′ → Y′ over Y, i.e. such that K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is an injection. Then the quotient map f/K : Y′/K → Y is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ-cohomologically smooth. Moreover, fixing the Λ-valued Haar measure on K with total volume 1 [Λ implicitly ℓ-power torsion, so that the indices [K : H] are invertible], there is a natural equivalence of functors Rf^! = q^* R(f/K)^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ), where q : Y′ → Y′/K is the quotient map.
items.note: S5: 'Prove 24.2 for free actions of a profinite group of pro-order prime to ℓ, including the normalized Λ-valued Haar measure and compatibility of finite-level traces.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target. See also source issue E100 (added by the review).

items.name: Remark after Proposition 24.2: Rq^! is not q^*
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 24.2 one also has Rf^! = Rq^! R(f/K)^!, but Rq^! ≠ q^* in general: after a base change q becomes S × Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, O_C) for a profinite set S and an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, and then Rq^!Λ is the sheaf sending an open and closed T ⊂ S to the distributions Hom(C⁰(T, Λ), Λ). A choice of Haar measure gives a natural map q^* → Rq^!.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S5 mentions this only as a caution ('do not assert Rq^! = q^*: the source explicitly describes a distribution-valued counterexample'); computing Rq^!Λ as distributions is not a stated target. The Haar-measure map q^* → Rq^! is part of the planned proof of 24.2.

items.name: Proposition 24.3: quotients by non-free profinite actions with smooth geometric fibres
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some prime ℓ ≠ p. Assume that there is a profinite group K of pro-order prime to ℓ with an action K × Y′ → Y′ over Y for which the map K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is 0-truncated and qcqs. Let Y′/K be the quotient of Y′ by the equivalence relation given as the image of K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′. Then f/K : Y′/K → Y is separated and representable in locally spatial diamonds. Moreover, if for all complete algebraically closed fields C with an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C and all maps Spa(C, C⁺) → Y the pullback Y′/K ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f/K is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and, fixing the Λ-valued Haar measure on K with total volume 1 (Λ ℓ-power torsion, which the paper leaves implicit, E100), there is a natural equivalence Rf^! = q^* R(f/K)^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ), where q : Y′ → Y′/K is the quotient map.
items.note: S5: 'Prove 24.3 in the nonfree case with its 0-truncated qcqs image-relation and fibrewise smoothness hypotheses. It is needed in the mixed-characteristic argument'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target. See also source issue E100 (added by the review).

items.name: Smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces and relative ball B^n_Y (Proposition 24.4)
items.statement: A separated morphism f : Y′ → Y of analytic adic spaces over Spa Z_p is smooth if it is locally on Y′ the composition of an étale map Y′ → B^n_Y and the projection B^n_Y → Y (cf. [Hub96, Cor. 1.6.10]); for Y = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, B^n_Y = Spa(A⟨T₁, …, T_n⟩, A⁺⟨T₁, …, T_n⟩).
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts: 'This is the notion smooth of ECD Proposition 24.4 for analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p'; comparison with Huber's smoothness: A2/smooth-local-ball-charts.

items.name: Proposition 24.4: smooth morphisms of analytic adic spaces are ℓ-cohomologically smooth
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over Spa Z_p, i.e. f is locally on Y′ the composition of an étale map Y′ → B^n_Y and the projection B^n_Y → Y. Then f^♢ : (Y′)^♢ → Y^♢ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth (for every prime ℓ ≠ p).
items.note: S5: 'Deduce 24.4 for separated smooth analytic adic morphisms over ℤ_p by local ball/torus presentations, characteristic-p comparison and the compatible-root ℤ_p-quotient argument.' Uses Lemma 15.6 (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/diamond-of-analytic-adic-space-and-etale-site-15-6), 22.3, 23.13, 24.1–24.3. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.5: (Spa Q_p)^♢ → * is ℓ-cohomologically smooth
items.statement: The map (Spa Q_p)^♢ → * is ℓ-cohomologically smooth (ℓ ≠ p).
items.note: S5: 'Deduce 24.5 for Spd ℚ_p → * using the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension and the punctured perfectoid disc.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.6: smoothness criterion over a general perfectoid base
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space, let Y be a locally spatial diamond, and let f : Y → X be compactifiable with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if (i) the sheaf Rf^!F_ℓ ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is invertible, i.e. étale locally isomorphic to F_ℓ[d] for some d ∈ Z; and (ii) for any X̃ → X that is an open subset of a finite-dimensional ball B^n_X over X, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ = Y ×_X X̃ → X̃, the natural transformation Rf̃^!F_ℓ ⊗^L_{F_ℓ} f̃^* → Rf̃^! of functors D_ét(X̃, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Ỹ, F_ℓ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S5: 'Prove the alternate geometric-base criterion 24.6.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 25.1: biduality over Spa(C, O_C)
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond that is separated and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spa(C, O_C) (structure map f) for some ℓ ≠ p. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) be a bounded complex with constructible cohomology. Then the double (naive) duality map A → RHom_{F_ℓ}(RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, F_ℓ), F_ℓ) is an equivalence; equivalently, as Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, the double Verdier duality map A → RHom_{F_ℓ}(RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, Rf^!F_ℓ), Rf^!F_ℓ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S6: 'Prove Theorem 25.1 ... Follow the reduction to j!𝔽_ℓ, strict-localization/approximation, the ball, and H5's smooth-curve compactification, keeping the actual biduality map throughout.' Inputs: Propositions 20.7, 20.8, 20.10, 23.17, Theorem 24.1, [Lüt95, Thm 5.3] (H5), Poincaré duality for curves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-poincare-duality). = Theorem 1.12. Nearest scheme analogue: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.1:biduality. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target. See also source issue E76 (added by the review).

items.name: Theorem 25.1 (final assertion): finiteness of cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond that is separated and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spa(C, O_C) (structure map f) for some ℓ ≠ p. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) be a bounded complex with constructible cohomology. If moreover X is quasicompact, then H^i(X, A) is finite for all i ∈ Z.
items.note: S6: 'Prove biduality and the finiteness of cohomology when X is quasicompact.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.2: biduality fails over Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C
items.statement: Theorem 25.1 does not hold with Spa(C, O_C) replaced by Spa(C, C⁺), C⁺ ≠ O_C, even for X = Spa(C, C⁺): if j : U = Spa(C, O_C) ↪ X denotes the open immersion, then A = j_!F_ℓ has dual RHom_{F_ℓ}(j_!F_ℓ, F_ℓ) = Rj_*F_ℓ = j_*F_ℓ = F_ℓ, so the double dual is F_ℓ, which is different from A = j_!F_ℓ.
items.note: S6: 'Implement the counterexample of Remark 25.2 over Spa(C,C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ 𝒪_C'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.3: biduality and perfectness for ℓ-power-torsion coefficients
items.statement: Let C, X be as in Theorem 25.1 and Λ an ℓ-power-torsion ring. The biduality theorem also holds for perfect-constructible A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), and in that case RΓ(X, A) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules if X is quasicompact.
items.note: S6: 'Prove the perfect-constructible extension to general ℓ-power-torsion commutative coefficients in Remark 25.3 ... The resulting perfect global-sections complex is a complex of coefficient-ring modules' (the print says 'A-modules'; see sourceIssues). Uses Proposition 20.17. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 25.4: conservativity of Verdier duality over Spa(C, O_C)
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond with f : X → Spa(C, O_C) compactifiable with locally dim.trg f < ∞. If A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) satisfies RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, Rf^!F_ℓ) = 0, then A = 0.
items.note: S6: 'Prove the Verdier dual conservativity assertion 25.4 in its stated compactifiable finite-dimensional setting.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.5: conservativity fails over Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C
items.statement: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C and i : {s} → X the inclusion of the closed point, RHom_Λ(i_*Λ, Λ) = 0 although i_*Λ ≠ 0.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S6 implements the analogous biduality counterexample (Remark 25.2) but does not name this one.

items.name: Remark 25.6: conservativity for general coefficient rings (conditional)
items.statement: A result similar to Proposition 25.4 holds with coefficients in a ring Λ killed by n prime to p as soon as every M ∈ D(Λ) with RHom_Λ(M, Λ) = 0 is zero. This fails in some cases, e.g. for Λ = O_K with K spherically complete and not discretely valued, and M = k the residue field (the paper omits "not discretely valued": for K = Q_p one has RHom_{Z_p}(F_p, Z_p) = F_p[−1] ≠ 0; E101).
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S6 only records that 'the general-ring conservativity discussion in Remark 25.6 is conditional, not an unconditional extension'; neither the conditional statement nor the counterexample is a stated target. See also source issue E101 (added by the review).

items.name: Adic coefficient rings (§26 setup)
items.statement: Λ is a ring complete for, and equipped with, the I-adic topology for a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ Λ; for simplicity I is assumed to be generated by a regular sequence and to contain an integer prime to p.
items.note: L0: 'Fix a commutative ring Λ complete for the I-adic topology, with I finitely generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0/derived-I-complete-etale-category. Mathlib has IsAdicComplete for modules (mathlib:IsAdicComplete) but not this coefficient formalism.

items.name: Definition 26.1: D_ét(Y, Λ) for adic coefficients
items.statement: For any small v-stack Y, D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_v, Λ) is the full subcategory of the derived category of Λ-modules on Y_v of all A ∈ D(Y_v, Λ) such that A is derived I-complete ([BS15, Def. 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.12]) and A ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I lies in D_ét(Y, Λ/I).
items.note: Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0/derived-I-complete-etale-category; derived completeness from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/derived-complete-sheaves. Footnote 8 notes the clash with D_ét(Y, Λ) for Λ discrete (L0: 'Distinguish this from D_ét for the same ring regarded as discrete').

items.name: Proposition 26.2: enhancement and inverse-limit description of adic D_ét
items.statement: There is a presentable stable ∞-category D_ét(Y, Λ) whose homotopy category is D_ét(Y, Λ), given as the full ∞-subcategory of D(Y_v, Λ) spanned by the objects of D_ét(Y, Λ). The natural functor D_ét(Y, Λ) → lim_n D_ét(Y, Λ/I^n) is an equivalence. However, D_ét(Y, Λ) → D(Y_v, Λ) does not preserve all colimits (so is not a map in Pr^L): colimits have to be completed in D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: L0: 'Prove Proposition 26.2 at the enhanced level: presentability/stability and equivalence with the inverse limit ... show that the uncompleted inclusion ... need not preserve them.' Nodes L0/derived-I-complete-etale-category, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/coefficient-system-reconstruction ([BS15, Lemma 3.5.7] without noetherianity), E4/completed-colimits.

items.name: Six operations for adic coefficients (§26)
items.statement: For f : Y′ → Y a morphism of small v-stacks: f^* : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ) is the restriction of f_v^* (it preserves completeness and reduction mod I); f^* preserves direct sums (checked mod I), hence has a right adjoint Rf_*; the completion of the tensor product on D(Y_v, Λ) gives a symmetric monoidal −⊗̂^L_Λ− on D_ét(Y, Λ), with adjoint RHom_Λ(−, −). If f is compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and locally dim.trg f < ∞, Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is defined by running the construction for the pro-system (Λ/I^n)_n and passing to the limit; it preserves arbitrary direct sums (and has an ∞-categorical enhancement), hence admits a right adjoint Rf^!.
items.note: L0: 'Construct the six operations for the entire coefficient system, then pass to the limit.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0/six-operations-for-adic-coefficients.

items.name: Remark 26.3: compatibility of the adic operations with reduction modulo I^n
items.statement: The functors f^*, Rf_! and −⊗̂^L_Λ− are compatible with the equivalence D_ét(Y, Λ) ≃ lim_n D_ét(Y, Λ/I^n). So are Rf_*, Rf^! and RHom_Λ(−, −): they commute with −⊗^L_Λ Λ/I and the corresponding operations on D_ét(Y, Λ/I) (I is generated by a regular sequence and they are exact), hence by induction with −⊗^L_Λ Λ/I^n, and are the limits of the operations for Λ/I^n. In particular, whether a natural transformation (e.g. a base change map) is an equivalence may be checked after replacing Λ by Λ/I; all results stated in the introduction hold for adic Λ.
items.note: L0: 'Prove the finite-level compatibility of all six operations, the regular-sequence/devissage argument for right adjoints and Hom, and the detection of equivalences modulo I.' Nodes L0/six-operations-for-adic-coefficients, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/mod-ideal-detection, E4/perfect-coefficient-change.

items.name: X^♢ and the comparison functor c_X^* for schemes of characteristic p
items.statement: For a scheme X of characteristic p, X^♢ is the small v-sheaf sending S ∈ Perf to the set of maps S → X in adic spaces, where schemes are embedded into adic spaces via Spec R ↦ Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ ⊂ R the integral closure of F_p; it factors over perfect schemes. This induces a functor of sites c_X : X^♢_v → X_ét and c_X^* : D(X_ét, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ) for any discrete ring Λ.
items.note: L1: 'For a scheme in characteristic p, construct the small v-sheaf of ECD §27 using its adic realization with the integral closure of 𝔽_p as the plus subring'. Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L1/char-p-scheme-diamond-and-comparison-functor.

items.name: Adic version: D_ét(X, Λ) ⊂ D(X_proét, Λ) and completed c_X^*
items.statement: For Λ adic (complete for an ideal I generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p), there is a map of sites c_X : X^♢_v → X_proét, and completed pullback gives c_X^* : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ), where D_ét(X, Λ) ⊂ D(X_proét, Λ) is the full subcategory of derived I-complete A ∈ D(X_proét, Λ) such that A ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I lies in the left completion D̂(X_ét) ⊂ D(X_proét) (equivalently, all cohomology sheaves lie in the essential image of X_ét^∼ ⊂ X_proét^∼); if D(X_ét) is left-complete (e.g. under finite cohomological dimension) this means A ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I ∈ D(X_ét).
items.note: L1: 'Construct the étale/pro-étale comparison morphisms of sites.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L1/char-p-scheme-diamond-and-comparison-functor.

items.name: Proposition 27.1: c_X^* commutes with tensor products and pullback
items.statement: The comparison functor c_X^* commutes with (i) the derived (completed) tensor product −⊗̂^L_Λ−; (ii) pullback: for any map f : Y → X of schemes of characteristic p, (f^♢)^* c_X^* = c_Y^* f^*.
items.note: L3: 'Construct the comparison pullback and right adjoint, and prove 27.1–27.3.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/commutation-and-adjoints-27-1-27-3.

items.name: Proposition 27.2(a): c_X^* has a right adjoint
items.statement: If X is any scheme of characteristic p, the functor c_X^* : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ) admits a right adjoint Rc_{X*}.
items.note: Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/full-faithfulness-27-2 (adjoint functor theorem, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations).

items.name: Proposition 27.2(b): c_X^* is fully faithful
items.statement: If X is any scheme of characteristic p, the functor c_X^* : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: L3: 'Full faithfulness of pullback in 27.2 is a theorem about the specified derived categories, not essential surjectivity ... Follow the reduction to perfected affine space, ... exhaustion by balls, finite-stage constructibility and the classical analytic comparison H5.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/full-faithfulness-27-2. Inputs: Theorem 19.5 (DiamondEtaleCohomology:C6), [Hub96, Prop. 6.1.1, Thm 3.8.1] (H5), scheme field-change invariance (missing, separate item).

items.name: Proposition 27.3: Rc_{X*} commutes with internal Hom and pushforward
items.statement: (i) For all A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), B ∈ D_ét(X^♢, Λ): Rc_{X*} RHom_Λ(c_X^* A, B) ≅ RHom_Λ(A, Rc_{X*} B). (ii) For all maps f : Y → X of schemes of characteristic p: Rf_* Rc_{Y*} ≅ Rc_{X*} Rf^♢_*.
items.note: Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/commutation-and-adjoints-27-1-27-3 (obtained by passing to right adjoints in 27.1).

items.name: Proposition 27.4(a): eligibility of f^♢ and Rf_! comparison (characteristic p)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated map of finite type of qcqs schemes of characteristic p, or the perfection thereof. Then f^♢ : Y^♢ → X^♢ is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and Rf^♢_! c_Y^* ≅ c_X^* Rf_!.
items.note: L3: 'Use L2 and S0–S3 to prove 27.4 ... Prove that its associated morphism is compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds and of finite dim.trg. Construct and prove the Rf! comparison'. Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/rf-shriek-comparison-27-4; Nagata: L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4; [Hub96, Thm 3.7.2]: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5/proper-comparison-3-7-2; scheme proper base change: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

items.name: Proposition 27.4(b): Rf^! comparison (characteristic p)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 27.4(a), Rf^! Rc_{X*} ≅ Rc_{Y*} R(f^♢)^!.
items.note: L3: 'then obtain the stated right-adjoint identity for exceptional pullback'. Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/rf-shriek-comparison-27-4.

items.name: X^♢ and c_X^* for schemes locally of finite type over a complete DVR
items.statement: Fix a complete discrete valuation ring O with perfect residue field k. For X locally of finite type over Spec O, X^♢ over Spd O sends a perfectoid space S of characteristic p to the set of untilts S^♯ over Spa O = Spa(O, O) together with a map S^♯ → X of locally ringed spaces over Spec O. (This is not compatible with the characteristic-p functor: Spec k ↦ Spd k = Spd(k, k), not Spd(k, k⁺).) One gets c_X^* : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ) satisfying Proposition 27.1, commuting with colimits, with right adjoint Rc_{X*} satisfying Proposition 27.3.
items.note: L1: 'Separately construct the mixed-characteristic version over a complete discrete valuation ring O with perfect residue field ... never identify the two by notation alone.' Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L1/mixed-characteristic-scheme-diamond.

items.name: Proposition 27.5(a): eligibility of f^♢ and Rf_! comparison over O
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated map between schemes of finite type over O. Then f^♢ : Y^♢ → X^♢ is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and Rf^♢_! c_Y^* ≅ c_X^* Rf_!.
items.note: L4: 'prove the geometric eligibility and Rf! comparison of 27.5 ... the analytic test space given by the locus x ≠ 0 in Spa O[[x]]'. Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L4/proper-support-comparison-27-5. See sourceIssues for the citation of 24.4 over the non-analytic Spa O.

items.name: Proposition 27.5(b): Rf^! comparison over O
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 27.5(a), Rf^! Rc_{X*} ≅ Rc_{Y*} R(f^♢)^!.
items.note: Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L4/proper-support-comparison-27-5 ('with its right-adjoint consequence').

items.name: Proposition 27.6: c_X^* commutes with Rf_* on constructible complexes
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated map between schemes of finite type over O, and assume that Λ is a finite ring killed by an integer prime to p. Then for any constructible complex A of Λ-modules on Y_ét, the map c_X^* Rf_* A → Rf^♢_* c_Y^* A is an isomorphism.
items.note: L6: 'Prove 27.6 for a separated map of schemes of finite type over O and a finite coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p'. Nodes AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L6/constructible-direct-image-comparison-27-6; alterations L5/de-jong-4-1-alteration-field-case, L5/de-jong-6-5-strictly-semistable-alteration.

items.name: Proposition 27.7: full faithfulness on constructible complexes over O
items.statement: Assume that Λ is a finite ring [the proof needs Λ killed by an integer prime to p]. Then for any scheme X locally of finite type over O and any constructible complex A of Λ-modules on X_ét, the adjunction map A → Rc_{X*} c_X^* A is an isomorphism.
items.note: L6: 'Prove the constructible full-faithfulness statement 27.7 in this standing prime-to-p coefficient setting ... The isolated wording finite ring in 27.7 is not used to claim a new p-torsion comparison'. Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L6/constructible-full-faithfulness-27-7. Index: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.6/scheme-adic-diamond-operation-comparisons-index.

items.name: [SGA 4 VI, Corollaire 5.2]: cohomology of coherent objects commutes with filtered colimits
items.statement: In a coherent topos, for a coherent (quasicompact quasiseparated) object U, the functors H^i(U, −) commute with filtered colimits of abelian sheaves; applied to the (κ-small) v-topos of a qcqs v-sheaf, RΓ commutes with arbitrary direct sums in D^{≥−n}.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 22.12, p. 135, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites: on a site with a generating full subcategory of qcqs objects stable under fibre products, 'for every qcqs object X and every i the natural map colim_j H^i(X, F_j) -> H^i(X, colim_j F_j) is an isomorphism' (SGA 4 VI 5.1–5.2 in the generality used: the v-topos of a qcqs v-sheaf). The consequence for direct sums in D^{≥−n} follows as in C9/global-sections-coproducts. SGA 4 is cited in the text but is not in the reference list. (Marked missing by the extraction; corrected by the review.)

items.name: [Lur09, §4.3.2 (Def. 4.3.2.2, Cor. 4.3.2.14)]: left Kan extensions along full embeddings
items.statement: For a full subcategory C₀ ⊂ C and F₀ : C₀ → D such that for each C ∈ C the diagram (C₀)_{/C} → D has a colimit, a left Kan extension F : C → D of F₀ exists, is computed pointwise by F(C) = colim_{(C₀)_{/C}} F₀, and is unique up to contractible choice (also in the relative setting over a base, e.g. coCartesian fibrations over Δ).
items.locator: Used in Definition 22.13, the construction before Lemma 22.16, and Lemma 22.16, pp. 135–137, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion (HTT 4.3.2.2, 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.16). Mathlib has only 1-categorical Kan extensions (CategoryTheory.Functor.LeftExtension), not the ∞-categorical statement.

items.name: [Lur09, Prop. 4.3.1.7]: colimits may be computed on a cofinal subdiagram
items.statement: As used: when computing the (relative) colimits defining a left Kan extension, one may restrict the indexing diagram along a cofinal map; the colimit exists for one iff for the other, and they agree.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 22.16, p. 137, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3 stage: 'Prove the cofinality result used when restricting from a total diagram to a fibre'; node E3/mates-and-beck-chevalley.

items.name: [Lur16, Prop. 1.4.4.1(2)]: coproduct-preserving exact functors preserve colimits
items.statement: An exact functor between stable ∞-categories admitting small colimits preserves all small colimits if and only if it preserves (small) coproducts/direct sums.
items.locator: Used in Propositions 22.14 and 22.20, pp. 135, 138, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations ('an EXACT functor between the relevant stable cocomplete categories PRESERVES ALL SMALL COLIMITS WHEN IT PRESERVES COPRODUCTS').

items.name: [LZ14, §2]: enhanced derived categories of diagrams of ringed topoi
items.statement: A diagram of ringed topoi gives a diagram of presentable symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories D(−, Λ) with pullback functors, functorially in the diagram.
items.locator: Used in the construction before Lemma 22.16, p. 136, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/coherent-diagrams-of-ringed-topoi ('FOLLOWING THE DIAGRAMMATIC CONSTRUCTION of Liu-Zheng, WITHOUT ASSUMING THEIR ARTIN-STACK SIX-OPERATION THEOREM').

items.name: [Nee96] (Neeman): compact objects and coproduct-preserving right adjoints
items.statement: Let F : T → T′ be an exact functor between triangulated categories, T compactly generated, with right adjoint G. Then G preserves arbitrary direct sums if and only if F preserves compact objects.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 23.7, p. 145, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nearest layers: DiamondSixOperations:S4 plans Proposition 23.7 ('the compactness/direct-sum criterion') and DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9 compact generation, but no stage or node states Neeman's criterion. Mathlib has triangulated categories but no compact objects or compact generation (no IsCompactObject-type declarations).

items.name: [FS26, Def. IV.3.1, Prop. IV.3.5]: formally smooth maps have local sections
items.statement: A formally smooth map (in the sense of [FS26, Def. IV.3.1]) has local sections after pullback to strictly totally disconnected spaces.
items.locator: Used in the remark after Remark 23.14, p. 150, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Stage VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1: 'Construct formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4'; the VS1 packet lists FS §IV.3 (formal smoothness) as remaining work of that layer. Only used to say that the compactifiability hypothesis of 23.13(b) is harmless in practice. (Marked missing by the extraction; corrected by the review.)

items.name: [Hub96, Theorem 6.2.2]: constructibility of R^j f_! for relative balls over finite-type bases
items.statement: For X_i topologically of finite type over Spa(K, O_K), the projection f_{X_i} : B × X_i → X_i of the relative closed unit ball, and a constructible sheaf F_i on B × X_i (torsion prime to p), the sheaves R^j f_{X_i!} F_i are constructible on X_i.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 24.1, condition (ii), p. 152, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Stage ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H4: 'Prove the instance of Hub96 Theorem 6.2.2 used for a relative ball over the finite-type bases approximating a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space.' No node yet.

items.name: [Hub96, Thm 7.5.3] and Poincaré duality for smooth curves
items.statement: For a smooth adic curve f : Y → S = Spa(C, C⁺) (C algebraically closed nonarchimedean, n prime to p) the trace Rf_!f^*(−)(1)[2] → id induces an isomorphism Rf_* RHom(G, f^*F(1)[2]) ≅ RHom(Rf_!G, F); in particular Rf^!F = f^*F(1)[2], compatibly with extension by zero from quasicompact opens of Spa(C, C⁺). (Used in 25.1 in the form: RΓ(U, F_ℓ) is dual to RΓ_c(U, Rf^!F_ℓ) for a quasicompact open U of a proper smooth curve over Spa(C, O_C).)
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 24.1, conditions (iii) and (iv), pp. 152–153; and (as 'Poincaré duality on U') in the proof of Theorem 25.1, p. 160, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-poincare-duality, H3/duality-open-extension-compatibility, H3/curve-duality-perfect-pairing, H3/curve-cohomology-finiteness; stage H3: 'The explicit Hub96 outputs are Proposition 5.5.8 (dimension bound), Theorem 7.2.2 (trace) and Theorem 7.5.3 (duality).'

items.name: [Hub96, Thm 7.2.2 and Prop. 5.5.8]: trace map for the ball over Spa(C, O_C)
items.statement: For the ball f_C : B × Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, O_C) one has R^i f_{C!} F_ℓ(1) = 0 for i > 2 (Prop. 5.5.8), and there is a trace map Rf_{C!} F_ℓ(1) → F_ℓ[−2] (Thm 7.2.2).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 24.1, condition (iv), p. 152, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-trace and H3/lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension (which says it is 'the form in which ECD's proof of Theorem 24.1 uses Hub96 Proposition 5.5.8'); H3/relative-ball-compact-support.

items.name: [Hub96, Cor. 1.6.10]: local structure of smooth morphisms
items.statement: A smooth morphism of (locally noetherian) analytic adic spaces is, locally on the source, the composite of an étale morphism to a relative closed polydisc B^n and the projection.
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts ('Huber's smooth morphisms are exactly the morphisms locally étale over a relative ball (Huber 1.6.10 globalised)').

items.name: [Lüt95, Theorem 5.3]: smooth rigid curves embed into proper smooth curves
items.statement: A (quasicompact) smooth rigid-analytic curve over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field C embeds as an open subspace into a proper smooth rigid-analytic curve.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Theorem 25.1, p. 160, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Stage ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5: 'Prove the compactification input used in ECD §25: the Lütkebohmert theorem cited as [Lüt95, Theorem 5.3] allowing the smooth rigid-curve reduction there to be embedded into a proper smooth rigid curve.' No node yet.

items.name: [BS15, Def. 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.12 and Lemma 3.5.7]: derived completeness and the inverse-limit description
items.statement: On a replete topos, K ∈ D(X, Λ) is derived I-complete if for all local sections x of I the derived limit of … →x K →x K vanishes; if I is generated by a regular sequence, the functor from derived I-complete objects D_comp(X, Λ) to lim_n D(X, Λ/I^n) (via −⊗^L_Λ Λ/I^n) is an equivalence (noetherianity of Λ not needed).
items.locator: Used in Definition 26.1 and the proof of Proposition 26.2, p. 162, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/derived-complete-sheaves, E4/coefficient-system-reconstruction ('No Noetherianity or boundedness is required'), AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0/derived-I-complete-etale-category. The decomposition's gap 'Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 3.5.5 and the non-noetherian extension of 3.5.7' records that the regular-sequence extension is not yet checked.

items.name: [Lur09, Prop. 5.5.3.13]: limits of presentable ∞-categories
items.statement: The ∞-category Pr^L of presentable ∞-categories and colimit-preserving functors admits small limits, computed in the ∞-category of ∞-categories; in particular a limit of presentable ∞-categories along colimit-preserving functors is presentable.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 26.2, p. 162, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nearest layers: AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L0 plans presentability of adic D_ét (26.2); EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5 node E5:presentability/presentable-categories defines presentable ∞-categories (HTT 5.5.0.1). Neither states HTT 5.5.3.13 itself.

items.name: [Hub96, Theorem 3.8.1 and Proposition 6.1.1]: algebraic–analytic comparison and finiteness
items.statement: (3.8.1) For a morphism f : X → Y of finite type of schemes locally of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field k and a constructible Z/nZ-sheaf F (n prime to char k), the base change maps φ_Y^* R^q f_* F → R^q f^{rig}_* φ_X^* F are isomorphisms. (6.1.1, as used) for the balls X_{C,n} over C and constructible c_X^*A with F_ℓ-coefficients, RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A) has finite total dimension (Huber's finiteness of cohomology of constructible sheaves on quasicompact spaces of finite type over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 27.2, p. 164, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: No node yet (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5/comparison-over-nonarchimedean-fields-3-8-1 is cited in the H0 packet but no H5 packet exists); stage H5: 'Prove the cases of Hub96 Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1, and Proposition 6.1.1, used in ECD §27'.

items.name: [Hub96, Theorem 3.7.2]: proper algebraic–analytic base change
items.statement: For f : X → Y proper between schemes locally of finite type over S, an adic space R with φ : R → S, and Λ torsion, the base change transformation φ_Y^* R^+f_* → R^+f^{ad}_* φ_X^* on D^+(X_ét, Λ) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Propositions 27.4 (p. 165) and 27.5 (p. 166), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Stage ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5: 'Prove the cases of Hub96 Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1, and Proposition 6.1.1, used in ECD §27: proper algebraic/analytic direct-image comparison'. No node yet (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5/proper-comparison-3-7-2 is cited in the H0 packet but no H5 packet exists).

items.name: Invariance of étale cohomology of schemes under extension of algebraically closed base field
items.statement: For a scheme X over an algebraically closed field k, an extension of algebraically closed fields C/k, and A ∈ D^+(X_ét, Λ) with Λ torsion prime to p, RΓ(X, A) ≅ RΓ(X_C, A).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 27.2, p. 164, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: The decomposition node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L3/full-faithfulness-27-2 lists it as an import 'not sourced in the read text'. Nearest layer: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (scheme étale cohomology, proper/smooth base change), which does not state it. The diamond analogue is ECD Theorem 19.5 (DiamondEtaleCohomology:C6).

items.name: Nagata compactification for separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes
items.statement: A separated morphism of finite type between qcqs schemes factors as an open immersion followed by a proper morphism; any two such factorisations are dominated by a third (the category of factorisations is filtered).
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Propositions 27.4 (p. 165), 27.5 (p. 166) and 27.6 (p. 167), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4; L2: 'This gives the nonnoetherian Nagata statement, not merely its finite-presentation special case.'

items.name: Proper base change for étale cohomology of schemes
items.statement: For a proper morphism of schemes and torsion coefficients, formation of Rf_* commutes with arbitrary base change (used for Spec C → Spec F̄_p and to reduce to F̄_p).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 27.4, p. 165, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2: 'construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support. Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers' (upstream PR196 EtaleBaseChange).

items.name: [dJ96, Theorems 4.1 and 6.5]: de Jong's alterations
items.statement: (4.1) For a variety X over a field k and a proper closed Z ⊂ X there is an alteration X₁ → X and an open immersion X₁ ⊂ X̄₁ with X̄₁ projective and regular such that the preimage of Z together with X̄₁ ∖ X₁ is a strict normal crossings divisor. (6.5) Over a complete DVR, after a finite extension of the base, a flat variety admits an alteration by a strictly semistable scheme (with strict normal crossings boundary).
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 27.6, pp. 166–167, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5/de-jong-4-1-alteration-field-case and L5/de-jong-6-5-strictly-semistable-alteration; L5 also plans the proper-hypercover descent the printed proof omits.

items.name: Localization Y_y of a spatial diamond or spatial v-sheaf at a point
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond (or a spatial v-sheaf) and y ∈ |Y|. The localization Y_y ⊂ Y of Y at y is the intersection of all quasicompact open subspaces of Y containing y. For any qcqs perfectoid space (resp. spatial diamond) Z over Y, with Z_y = Z ×_Y Y_y, quasicompact open subspaces of Z_y come via pullback from quasicompact open subspaces of Z ×_Y U for some quasicompact open subspace U ⊂ Y containing y, and any two such extensions agree after shrinking U.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 11.21, p. 62; also proofs of Lemma 11.31, p. 69, and Lemma 12.16, p. 73; used again in §20, pp. 116 and 120, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Added by the independent review. Paper text: 'Let Y_y ⊂ Y be the localization of Y at y, i.e. the intersection of all quasicompact open subspaces containing y. For any qcqs perfectoid space Z over Y, let Z_y = Z ×_Y Y_y. Then quasicompact open subspaces of Z_y come via pullback from quasicompact open subspaces of Z ×_Y U for some quasicompact open subspace U of Y, and any two such extensions agree after shrinking U.' |Y_y| is the set of generalizations of y, pro-constructible and generalizing, so Y_y is spatial by Propositions 11.20 and 12.15. Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/injection-and-finite-etale-permanence ('localise at a point y') and D5/local-structure-of-etale-maps ('base change to the localization Y_y') use it as a proof step, but no stage or node states the construction or its spreading-out property, so it is missing; it goes with route 1 (D5).

items.name: Proof of Proposition 14.8: Pro(Y_ét,qc,sep) is a basis of Y_qproét
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and Y_ét,qc,sep ⊂ Y_ét the full subcategory of quasicompact separated étale maps. Then Y_ét,qc,sep is a basis for the topology of Y_ét, so Y_ét,qc,sep^∼ ≅ Y_ét^∼. The functor Pro(Y_ét,qc,sep) → Y_qproét, “lim” Ỹ_j ↦ lim Ỹ_j, is fully faithful, and its essential image forms a basis for the topology of Y_qproét; hence ν_Y may be replaced by Pro(Y_ét,qc,sep) → Y_ét,qc,sep, and for a sheaf F on Y_ét and Ỹ = lim_j Ỹ_j ∈ Pro(Y_ét,qc,sep) one has (ν_Y^*F)(Ỹ) = colim_j F(Ỹ_j) (as in Proposition 8.5).
items.note: Added by the independent review. Planned only at stage level, as the proof of 14.8 ('Prove 14.4–14.11 …'; C0 also asks for 'comparison with the respective bases of perfectoid objects'). Inputs: Convention 10.2, Corollary 11.28, Proposition 11.23(iii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons), Proposition 11.24, and the affinoid-perfectoid analogue Proposition 7.10 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence). No node states the diamond version. Reused by name in Proposition 14.9, Theorem 14.12(i) and Proposition 16.6.

prerequisites.citation: A. Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer. III. Exemples et compléments, in: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 3, North-Holland (1968), 88–188

routes.reason: D0 is the layer that builds the spectral-space and coherent-topos foundations the whole paper rests on ('Build the missing coherent and algebraic topos interfaces … exactness of sheafification and filtered colimits … derived global sections'). It is where the profiniteness of π₀ of a spectral space, the reduction of cofiltered limits to ordinal-indexed ones (used in 11.22, 11.23, 12.17), the flasque constant sheaf on a spectral space with a generic point ([Sta 02UW], used in 13.13) and SGA 4 VI.8.7.7 on limits of coherent topoi (for 14.9) belong; SGA 4 VI 5.2 (for 22.12, item 598) is already planned by node D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites, and the paper is a source for it; D1, D4 and D5 already use them in proof steps. D5 takes the localization Y_y of a spatial diamond at a point (item 618, added by the review), which its nodes use in proof steps but never state. The three algebraic inputs to Lemma 9.5 do not belong to D3: the DiamondsAndVStacks packet records them as 'not planned in this packet'. They go to their owners: the fppf refinement (208) to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (route 5), Raynaud–Gruson over valuation rings of any height (209) to AdicSpacesPartII:R2 (route 6), and the lifting of special-fibre points (210) is planned by AdicSpacesPartII:R2/specialisation-map.

Statements of §§17–20 that the paper asserts in running text or as a remark, and that the owning layers need: the D⁺ formula for R_Yét and the comparison of Rf_* with the left-completed étale pushforward (C2, C3, which plan D_ét and Rf_*), the locally-compact-Hausdorff characterisation of proper maps in Remark 18.2(b) (C4, proper and partially proper maps), and Proposition 20.14, which C7's plan for 20.15–20.16 uses but no node states.

The remarks of §§23–25 that bound the six-operation statements: descent of representability along universally open covers (S4), the distribution-valued computation showing Rq^! ≠ q^* (S5), and the failure and conditional extension of conservativity (S6). S4–S6 plan the corresponding theorems; S5 and S6 mention Rq^! ≠ q^* and Remark 25.6 only as cautions, and no stage states Remark 23.14 or Remark 25.5. The formal-smoothness input (item 604) is planned by VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS1 and is not routed.

General ∞-categorical inputs used in Lemmas 17.1 and 17.8, Proposition 26.2 and Proposition 23.7. EnhancedDerivedSheaves E3 owns adjoint functor theorems and localisations and E5:presentability's node presentable-categories defines presentable ∞-categories and states the representability criterion (HTT 5.5.2.2, so item 406 is planned and named here as a planned item); neither yet states HTT 5.5.3.12–13 (items 407 and 611, which should be planned together) or Neeman's criterion that a right adjoint preserves coproducts when the left adjoint preserves compact objects.

SF.2 is the layer that is to 'construct sheaf cohomology, localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support' for schemes. The paper uses scheme proper base change in Lemma 19.4 and invariance of étale cohomology under extension of algebraically closed base field in Proposition 27.2, and (in Lemma 9.5) the refinement of fppf covers of strictly henselian local rings by finite flat ones [Gro68], a scheme-theoretic input that SF.2 owns with its fppf and étale site comparisons ('Own Zariski, etale, fppf and pro-etale site comparisons'). Scheme proper base change (441) is planned by SF.2 itself and is named here as a planned item; the atlas's comparison layer AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L3 lists the latter as an unsourced import.

Added by the review, from route 1. R2 owns formal schemes over valuation rings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 defers formal schemes to AdicSpacesPartII). Node R2/flat-tft-is-tfp proves that a flat topologically finite type O_K-algebra is topologically finitely presented for a complete rank-one O_K, and its hypotheses already mention the any-height form (Fujiwara–Kato I, Corollary 2.3.2); Lemma 9.5 needs it over C⁺ of any height (item 209), so R2's blueprint must state it in that generality. The lifting of special-fibre points to O_C-points (item 210) is planned by R2/specialisation-map (iii) and is named here as a planned item.

sourceIssues.locator: proof of Lemma 2.9 (existence of generic points), p. 13 (arXiv:1709.07343v4, 14 April 2026)
sourceIssues.printed: The source considers the cofiltered family of opens U ⊂ X/R satisfying U ∩ Z ≠ ∅ and having quasicompact preimage in X. To establish existence, it seeks a point in their intersection. Each preimage is open and quasicompact, hence compact Hausdorff in the constructible topology. It argues that their nonemptiness makes their intersection nonempty, and consequently the U’s also have a nonempty intersection.
sourceIssues.correction: Intersect with Z. With π : X → X/R, the sets π⁻¹(U) ∩ π⁻¹(Z), for basic opens U meeting Z, are closed in the constructible topology of X (π⁻¹(U) is quasicompact open, π⁻¹(Z) is closed, hence pro-constructible), nonempty, and cofiltered (U₁ ∩ U₂ ∩ Z ≠ ∅ by irreducibility of Z, and the basis is stable under finite intersections). By compactness of the constructible topology they have a common point x. Then π(x) ∈ Z lies in every basic open meeting Z, so it is a generic point of Z.
sourceIssues.reason: A point of the intersection of the U’s need not lie in Z, so nonemptiness of that intersection does not give a generic point of Z. Example within the lemma’s hypotheses: X = X/R = Spec of a DVR {η, s}, R the diagonal, Z = {s}; the only open meeting Z is the whole space, so the intersection is {η, s} and contains η ∉ Z. (The conclusion of the lemma is unaffected: the repaired argument is the same compactness argument with π⁻¹(Z) added.)

review.reason: The image of p. 13 prints exactly the quoted argument: it proves only that the intersection of the basic opens U meeting Z is nonempty, which does not give a point of Z. I checked the counterexample: X = Spec of a DVR = {η, s}, R the diagonal (pro-constructible, s = t = id generalizing, X/R = X has the required basis), Z = {s}; the only open meeting Z is X, so the intersection is {η, s} ∋ η ∉ Z. The repair (add the pro-constructible set π⁻¹(Z), cofilteredness from irreducibility, then a point of Z in every basic open meeting Z is generic) is correct; the lemma stands.

sourceIssues.locator: proof of Lemma 2.10 (existence of generic points), p. 13 (arXiv:1709.07343v4, 14 April 2026)
sourceIssues.printed: The source seeks a generic point for each irreducible closed Z̄ ⊂ X/R. It identifies this with nonemptiness of the intersection of the quasicompact opens V0 ⊂ X/R satisfying V0 ∩ Z̄ ≠ ∅. Compactness in the constructible topology is then used to make the intersection of their preimages in X nonempty and to conclude the claim.
sourceIssues.correction: Equivalently, the intersection of Z̄ with all quasicompact open V₀ ⊂ X/R meeting Z̄ (and having quasicompact preimage) is nonempty. This follows from compactness of the constructible topology of the (reduced to quasicompact, hence spectral) X applied to the cofiltered family of nonempty constructibly closed sets π⁻¹(V₀) ∩ π⁻¹(Z̄); a point of Z̄ in all such V₀ is a generic point since these V₀ form a basis.
sourceIssues.reason: The asserted equivalence is false as a logical step: a point in the intersection of the V₀ need not lie in Z̄, and then it does not give a generic point of Z̄ (same Spec-of-a-DVR example as for Lemma 2.9: the intersection is the whole space for Z̄ = {s}). The repair is immediate by adding π⁻¹(Z̄), which is pro-constructible.

sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts R° ⊂ ⋃_{k≥0} Φ^{−k}(R₀), from which it deduces R° ⊂ ϖ^{−n}R₀ and the required boundedness.
sourceIssues.correction: Only topologically nilpotent elements are covered: for x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so (ϖx)^{p^k} ∈ R₀ for k ≫ 0, i.e. ϖR° ⊂ ⋃_k Φ^{−k}(R₀). Together with a uniform bound ⋃_k Φ^{−k}(R₀) ⊂ ϖ^{−c}R₀ (proved with integral exponents, see PerfectoidSpaces/E7 for the preceding fractional-exponent step) this gives R° ⊂ ϖ^{−1−c}R₀, so R° is bounded.
sourceIssues.reason: The inclusion fails for an arbitrary open bounded subring R₀: take K the completion of 𝔽_{p²}((t^{1/p^∞})), R₀ = 𝔽_p + tK° (open, bounded subring), and λ ∈ 𝔽_{p²} \ 𝔽_p. Then λ ∈ K° but λ^{p^k} ∈ {λ, λ^p} ⊄ R₀ for all k (elements of R₀ have constant term in 𝔽_p), so λ ∉ ⋃_k Φ^{−k}(R₀). The proposition itself is true (uniformity of perfect complete Tate rings is standard).

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 4.4 and its proof, pp. 20–21 (arXiv:1709.07343v4, 14 April 2026)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 4.4 characterizes κ-small perfectoid X by a covering with fewer than κ open affinoids U = Spa(A, A+), each having A of cardinality below κ. It further asserts that such a covering forces the cardinality of |X| to be below κ.
sourceIssues.correction: For the 'if' direction require fewer than cf(κ) covering affinoids (e.g. countably many, since cf κ > ω), or a uniform bound sup #A < κ, or κ regular; without this one only gets that every open affinoid has ring of cardinality < κ. The finite-product addendum likewise needs uniformly bounded (e.g. quasicompact) factors.
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 4.1 allows singular κ, e.g. κ = κ(ω₁) of cofinality ω₁ < κ (and the paper says an uncountable strong limit suffices in §4). Let K_α (α < ω₁) be perfectoid fields with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ; the disjoint union of the perfectoid closed discs over the K_α is covered by ω₁ < κ affinoids whose rings have cardinality < κ, but it has at least sup #K_α = κ points (its classical points), so it is not κ-small. (For the finite-product addendum the atlas finding PerfectoidSpaces/E40 gives a separate example: a disjoint union of ω₁ field points Spa(K_α) over a fixed field is κ-small, but its self-product has unboundedly many points.)

review.reason: Text pp. 20–21 matches the quote. Lemma 4.1's κ(µ) for µ = ω₁ has cofinality ω₁ < κ, so it is singular, and the paper says §4 needs only an uncountable strong limit. I rebuilt the counterexample: perfectoid fields K_α (α < ω₁) with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ (#K_α ≤ 2^{λ_α} < κ by Remark 4.3); the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs over the K_α is covered by ω₁ affinoids with rings of size < κ, but has at least sup #K_α = κ classical points. review.reason: Text p. 29: the proof asserts 'As (R, R+) is perfectoid' for the completed colimit with no argument, and integral closedness of R⁺ in R is also not addressed. Both are true. Frobenius on R⁺/ϖ is a filtered colimit of isomorphisms (up to almost), and completion of a ring of integral elements stays integrally closed (standard, e.g. Huber's completion lemma or Bhatt's notes). review.reason: Text p. 29: 'write (R, R+) as the (automatically ω1-filtered) colimit of all perfectoid (Ri, Ri+) ⊂ (R, R+) that admit a countable dense subset.' The proof neither shows that every countable subset of R lies in such a subring nor that countably many of them have a common upper bound. The subring generated by two perfectoid subrings need not be perfectoid, so a countable-hull construction is needed. Gap in the proof; the statement is true.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 7.2(iii) calls the sheaf functor F ↦ Γ(X, F) exact, explaining exactness as preservation of every finite colimit.
sourceIssues.correction: (iii) The functor F ↦ Γ(X, F) on sheaves (of sets) on X commutes with coequalizers. This is exactly what the proof of (i)⇒(iii) establishes ('We have to see that Γ(X, −) commutes with coequalizers') and what (iii)⇒(iv) uses (cokernels of abelian sheaves are coequalizers of sheaves of sets). Γ preserves finite coproducts only when X is connected.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: X = {a, b} with the discrete topology is spectral and every open cover splits (each component is a point), so (i) and (ii) hold. Sheaves on X are pairs of sets and Γ(X, F) = F_a × F_b. For F = G = the terminal sheaf, Γ(X, F ⊔ G) has 4 elements while Γ(X, F) ⊔ Γ(X, G) has 2, so Γ does not commute with finite colimits. In general Γ(X, F ⊔ G) = ⊔ over clopen decompositions X = U ⊔ V of F(U) × G(V).

sourceIssues.printed: The source claims a left adjoint X ↦ X^wl for the inclusion of w-local perfectoid spaces, with w-local morphisms, into qcqs perfectoid spaces. It calls X^wl → X the adjunction map and asserts that it is pro-étale.
sourceIssues.correction: … admits a right adjoint X ↦ X^wl. The counit X^wl → X is pro-étale.
sourceIssues.reason: An adjunction map X^wl → X from the w-local object to X is the counit of ι ⊣ (−)^wl, i.e. (−)^wl is right adjoint to the inclusion ι; a left adjoint L would come with a unit X → ιL(X). The proof confirms the right-adjoint property: X^wl is 'final in the category of w-local perfectoid spaces over X (with w-local maps)', i.e. Hom_wl(Z, X^wl) = Hom(Z, X); the text before Definition 7.8 calls X^wl → X 'a universal map … from a w-local space'. This matches [BS15, Lemma 2.1.10], where the w-localization is a right adjoint. The meaning is clear from the proof, so the slip affects nothing.

sourceIssues.printed: The source considers f, g : T_1 → T_2 between the factorizations under consideration and asserts that their equality locus T ⊂ T_1 is clopen. More specifically, from T_1 = ⊔_{i∈I} U_i it obtains T = ⊔_{i∈J} U_i for a subset J ⊂ I, and says X^wl → T_1 factors over T.
sourceIssues.correction: T ∩ U_i is an open and closed subset of U_i, not necessarily ∅ or U_i, so T need not be a union of members U_i (and, for an arbitrary basis B, need not be an object of C). To equalize f and g inside C: cover the quasicompact open T by finitely many B_k ∈ B, note that the cover {B_k} of T splits after pullback to the w-local space X^wl, and use T′ = ⊔_k B_k → T ⊂ T_1. (For B = rational subsets of an affinoid perfectoid space, clopen subsets of rational subsets are rational, so T itself lies in C.)
sourceIssues.reason: A map U_i → T_2 = ⊔_j V_j over X is the same as a decomposition of U_i into clopen pieces W_j ⊂ V_j, so f and g can agree on a proper clopen part of a disconnected U_i. Example: X = {a, b} discrete, B = all subsets, T_1 = T_2 = X ⊔ X with X^wl = X mapping to the first copies, f = id, g = id on the first copy and on the second copy sending a to a but b to the first copy; then T = (first copy) ⊔ {a} is not a union of the U_i. The conclusion 'C is cofiltered' remains true by the argument in the correction.

sourceIssues.printed: The source reduces to affinoid Z and asserts that every continuous map |Z| → T, with T compact Hausdorff, factors through the profinite component set π0(Z).
sourceIssues.correction: Replace 'affinoid' by '(strictly) totally disconnected' (allowed, since one is looking for a pro-étale cover Z̃ → Z anyway: Lemma 7.18 gives an affinoid pro-étale strictly totally disconnected cover). Then each connected component of |Z| is |Spa(K′, K′⁺)|, which has a dense generic point, so any continuous map to the Hausdorff space T is constant on it; since |Z| → π₀(Z) is a quotient map onto a profinite set, |Z| → T factors continuously through π₀(Z), and the rest of the argument (Z̃ = Z ×_{π₀(Z)} (π₀(Z) ×_T S)) is unchanged. The claimed full faithfulness is unaffected.
sourceIssues.reason: The assertion is false for general affinoid Z. Take Z = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), the perfectoid closed unit disc over K. Its ring of global functions is a domain (the Gauss norm is multiplicative), so |Z| has no nontrivial clopen subsets and π₀(Z) is a point. By the paper's own Proposition 13.9, |Z| → |Z|_B is a continuous surjection onto a compact Hausdorff space, and |Z|_B is not a point (the Gauss point and the point T = 0 give different seminorms). So with T = |Z|_B, the element of T(Z) = C⁰(|Z|, T) given by this map, that is a map Z → T × Spa(K, O_K), does not factor through π₀(Z).

sourceIssues.printed: The source reduces the task to proving an isomorphism Spa(C, O_C) → Y_0°. It defines Y_0° ⊂ Y_0 as the open subfunctor attached to the maximal point and declares that point open.
sourceIssues.correction: The maximal point η of |Y_0| need not be open. Take Y_0° := Y_0 ×_{|Y_0|} {η} instead. The set {η} is the intersection of the quasicompact opens containing η, so it is pro-constructible and generalizing, and Y_0° → Y_0 is a quasicompact injection: a spatial diamond by Proposition 11.20, or a sub-v-sheaf as in Proposition 12.15 for 12.20. R_0° = R_0 ×_{Y_0} Y_0° is then the fibre of R_0 over the rank-one point of Spa(C, C⁺), namely S × Spa(C, O_C). The rest of the argument (the profinite group G, the finite étale covers and their extension to a clopen subset of Y) never uses openness.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: Y = Y_0 = Spa(C, C⁺), which is strictly totally disconnected and so satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition 11.26. Here C⁺ ⊂ O_C is the preimage of a valuation ring W of the residue field k of C whose value group is ⊕_{n≥1} ℚ, ordered by the sign of the last nonzero coordinate. Such W exist, e.g. for C the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) with k an algebraic closure of 𝔽_p(x_1, x_2, …), using the monomial valuation. The convex subgroups H_n = ⊕_{i≤n} ℚ increase and exhaust the group, so the points of Spa(C, C⁺) form the chain C⁺ ⊂ V_1 ⊂ V_2 ⊂ … ⊂ O_C with ⋃_n V_n = O_C. A rational subset containing the rank-one point has the form {V : h_1, …, h_m ∈ V} with h_j ∈ O_C, and all the h_j already lie in some V_N ≠ O_C. So no open set is {O_C}: the maximal point is not open.

sourceIssues.locator: proof of Proposition 14.7 (vanishing of R^iλ_{Y*}λ_Y^*F), p. 85 (arXiv:1709.07343v4, 14 April 2026)
sourceIssues.printed: The source chooses the least failing i and a nonzero α ∈ H^i(X_v, λ∗_Y F). A v-cover f : X′ → X kills α, and X′ is assumed affinoid perfectoid. It then uses a Čech spectral sequence to obtain α from a differential-kernel class in (λ∗_Y F)(X′ ×X . . . ×X X′), with i + 1 copies of X′.
sourceIssues.correction: For i ≥ 2 the passage to a Čech cocycle needs H^q((X′ ×_X ⋯ ×_X X′)_v, λ_Y^*F) = 0 for 0 < q < i (with at least two factors), or at least the vanishing of the corresponding E_∞-terms. Minimality of i gives vanishing only on strictly totally disconnected spaces. On the fibre powers, minimality and Proposition 14.8 only identify these groups with H^q_ét, which the proof does not show to vanish. An extra argument is needed, for example vanishing of these étale groups for a suitable choice of X′, or a hypercover form of the approximation-and-splitting step. The case i = 1, and so the statement for sheaves of groups, is unaffected.
sourceIssues.reason: In the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence E₁^{p,q} = H^q((X′^{×_X(p+1)})_v, λ_Y^*F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_v, λ_Y^*F), the hypothesis f^*α = 0 only removes the E^{0,i}-component of α. α lies in the Čech part E^{i,0} only if its components in E^{p,i−p}, 1 ≤ p ≤ i−1, vanish. The fibre powers are affinoid perfectoid but in general not strictly totally disconnected. For example, take X = Spa(C, O_C) and X′ = Spa(C′, O_{C′}) with C′ the completed algebraic closure of the Gauss-norm completion of C(t). Then X′ ×_X X′ is connected (Lemma 14.6) but has two rank-one points on which |t⊗1 − 1⊗t| is 0 and 1 respectively. So it is not of the form Spa(K, K⁺), and the induction hypothesis does not apply to it.

sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that quasiseparated X implies quasiseparated X → ∗, using algebraicity of T and SGA 4 VI Proposition 2.2. It also claims quasicompact X → ∗ implies quasicompact X by SGA 4 VI Proposition 1.3: choosing any quasicompact Y ∈ T, it regards X × Y → X as a cover and X × Y as quasicompact whenever X → ∗ is quasicompact.
sourceIssues.correction: X → ∗ quasicompact implies X quasicompact provided the final object ∗ is covered by some quasicompact object Y (Y → ∗ surjective); then X × Y → X is a cover by a quasicompact object. This holds for (small) sheaves on Perfd, since every perfectoid space pro-étale-locally maps to the quasicompact Spa(ℚ_p^cycl) ⊔ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧), and on X_proét for quasicompact X, but not for X_proét with X not quasicompact.
sourceIssues.reason: X × Y → X is a cover only if Y → ∗ is surjective (for Y = ∅ it is not), and the implication fails in general algebraic topoi. Counterexample in one of the paper's own settings (algebraic by Proposition 8.3): T = small sheaves on X_proét for X = ⊔_{n∈ℕ} Spa(C, O_C). The final object is X, so X → ∗ is the identity and quasicompact, but X is not quasicompact (its cover by the components has no finite subcover). In the cases used later (sheaves on Perfd/Perf) the corrected hypothesis holds, so later uses are unaffected.

sourceIssues.printed: The source reduces verification to stalks and chooses y ∈ |Y|^B. It asserts cofinality of the clopen neighborhoods of y and uses a standard limit argument to deduce (Rf∗f∗F)_y = RΓ(f⁻¹(y), f∗F).
sourceIssues.correction: Open and closed neighbourhoods of y are cofinal only when |Y|^B is totally disconnected (e.g. profinite). What is true, and presumably intended (cf. the proof of Lemma 2.6, 'the open neighborhoods are cofinal with the closed neighborhoods'), is that closed neighbourhoods are cofinal and, as f : |Y| → |Y|^B is closed (quasicompact source, Hausdorff target), the sets f⁻¹(U) are cofinal among the open neighbourhoods of the fibre f⁻¹(y). The identity (Rf∗G)_y = RΓ(f⁻¹(y), G|) then needs a separate justification, e.g. a tautness statement for the closed quasicompact subset f⁻¹(y) ⊂ |Y| (colim_{W ⊃ f⁻¹(y)} H^i(W, G) = H^i(f⁻¹(y), G)), or a reduction to a profinite base via a surjection S → |Y|^B and Y ×_{|Y|^B} S (spatial, Proposition 13.12) together with descent along S → |Y|^B. The text supplies neither.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to the cofinality claim within the hypotheses: Y = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is affinoid perfectoid, hence a quasicompact separated diamond. Its ring is a domain (multiplicative Gauss norm), so |Y| is connected, and |Y|^B, a continuous image of |Y| (Proposition 13.9), is connected; it has at least two points (the Gauss point and the point T = 0 differ on |T|). In a connected Hausdorff space with two points the only open and closed neighbourhood of y is the whole space, which is not inside the open neighbourhood of y missing the other point, so open and closed neighbourhoods are not cofinal. The same happens for T̲ × Spa(K, O_K) with T = [0, 1] (Example 11.12). I have not found the conclusion of 13.13 to fail; only the step is unsupported.
